Get started

Take a tour of the app#

You will find your way around the app, move from one screen to another without searching, and read what the top bar tells you. Five minutes, free.

Deepotus Video Gen is a studio that runs on your own computer. It turns an idea into a video, a picture, a 3D object or a published post. You plug in your own AI provider keys: you pay those providers, not the app. Everything you create stays with you.

The screen at a glance#

  1. The rail, on the left: one screen per task. Quick for a one-click video, Studio to compose, Edit to cut a video, Library to find your media, Settings for the keys. The arrow at the top of the rail folds it into icons only.
  2. The quick command: click Quick command… or press Ctrl+K, type a few letters, Enter.
  3. The spending counter shows what you spent this month with your providers. One click opens Settings.
  4. The badges fal, heygen and voice turn green when the matching key is set. One click takes you to that key.
  5. The render queue, top right, lists what is being computed and what just finished, in the Running and Recent tabs.

Go fast with the quick command#

The quick command goes to any screen (Go to Studio, Go to News…), opens the last render, creates a starter graph or opens a Settings section. Replay onboarding restarts the first-launch tour.

The screens of the rail#

Quick

A one-click video: animated clip, talking avatar, composition, voiceover.

Studio

A node graph to compose a video piece by piece.

Chapters

From a text or a novel to a narrated video, scene by scene.

Sound & VFX

Music, voices, sound effects and visual effects.

Edit

A multitrack timeline to cut, grade and deliver.

Scheduler

Plan and publish your posts for the week.

Templates

Reusable layouts and your brand kits.

News

Follow the news and turn it into short videos.

Library

All your pictures, renders, sounds and objects, with their origin.

Game Assets

3D, sprites, tiles, materials and playing cards.

Vectorlab

Vector drawing, pixel art, maps and printable objects.

Photolab

Photo retouching with layers, masks and filters.

The guide opens from the foot of the rail: FR or EN.

What the app does to protect you#

Nothing leaves without you

Only this PC can change, generate or spend. Another device on the network can only read, and only once paired.

Errors that make sense

A missing key or a server refusal is shown in plain words, with what to do.

Safe imports

A picture with the same name becomes name-1, name-2…; a file that is not a real picture is refused and named.

In-app dialogs

Confirmations and text prompts use one Deepotus dialog, never a browser pop-up.

Good to know#

The desktop icon opens the app at http://deepotus.localhost:8765. Each browser tab carries the name of the open tool, for example “Deepotus — Vectorlab”.

Only AI generations cost money, and your provider bills them. The chapter Keep spending under control shows how to set limits.

Shortcuts#

KeyEffect
Ctrl+KOpens the quick command
EscCloses the quick command or a dialog
Get started

Install, pick a language, update#

You will launch the app for the first time, pick its language, know what each use costs and keep it up to date. Ten minutes, free.

First launch#

  1. During installation, pick the language: French or English. It becomes the language of the whole app.
  2. Double-click the Deepotus Video Gen desktop icon. The app starts without a black window, then your browser opens on the studio.
  3. On the very first launch, a five-step welcome introduces the studio and lets you pick a persona, your generation providers and the networks you publish to.
  4. Set at least one key, the fal.ai one: it makes pictures and video clips. The chapter Connect your keys shows how.

The welcome can be replayed at any time from the quick command (Ctrl+K): Replay onboarding.

Switch language#

  1. Open Settings › Provider defaults.
  2. In Interface language, pick Français or English. The page reloads in the chosen language.

Translated: the sidebar, Settings, the Library, Quick, News, the Scheduler, the Studio, Templates, Episodes, the editor, Sound & VFX, subtitles, machine transfer and every confirmation dialog. Lists sent by the server (effects, transitions, presets) also arrive in the chosen language. The labs (Vectorlab, Photolab, Card Forge…) are being translated one by one; meanwhile their known texts are translated on display. What you type yourself is never translated.

What each use costs#

The app is free. Only AI generations cost money, billed by the provider of the key. Rough figures at default rates:

ActionProviderIndicative cost
Create a picturefal.ai (FLUX)≈ $0.003
10 s video clipfal.ai (Seedance 2.5, 720p)≈ $4.73
Talking avatar, 1 minHeyGen≈ $0.24
VoiceoverElevenLabsper character, free tier available
News summary, post planAnthropic, OpenAI, Gemini or Ollamaa few cents, free with Ollama
Import your videos, sounds, picturesnonefree

Your real rates go into Settings › Pricing & budget; see Keep spending under control.

Keep the app up to date#

  1. Once a day, the app checks whether a new version is published. It never blocks anything.
  2. When there is one, a card announces it: Download fetches the installer and shows where it is saved, Later hides the card for that version, Notes tells what changes.
  3. To check right now: Settings › Diagnostics, Check button.
  4. Close the app, run the downloaded installer: nothing is installed on its own.

Good to know#

Your keys, files and database live in the %LOCALAPPDATA%\DeepotusVideoGenData folder, apart from the program: they survive updates and reinstalls.

Start with the fal.ai key alone, then add avatars, voices and AI as you go. Set a monthly cap from day one: see Keep spending under control.

Get started

Connect your keys and AI engines#

You will set an AI provider's key, choose which engine does what, connect a free provider or a server on your network, and protect your keys with a password. Ten minutes, free; keys are created with each provider.

Before you start#

An API key is a code the provider gives you on its website, in your account. It lets the app work on your behalf; the provider bills you. Only one is required to start: fal.ai.

Set a key#

  1. Open Settings › API keys. Each provider has its row and its status: missing until a key is set. The fal, heygen and voice badges in the header lead here in one click.
  2. Click Guide: it tells where to create the key with the provider and how it is billed.
  3. Paste the key in the field, then Save. It works right away, no restart.
  4. Click Test on the row: the provider says whether it accepts the key, without spending anything.

To set several keys at once, fill in the fields then Save all changes.

Which key unlocks what#

KeyWhat it unlocks
fal.aiPictures (FLUX) and video clips (Seedance). The only key you need.
HeyGenTalking avatars, alone or in a composition.
ElevenLabsVoiceover and narration; two fields set the default French and English voices.
Anthropic, OpenAI or GeminiNews summaries, post plans, scripts and storyboards written by AI. One is enough; OpenAI also makes pictures (GPT Image).
Free provider (DeepSeek, OpenRouter, Mistral, Groq…)The same texts, from a service that speaks the OpenAI API. Price to be measured.
Local servers (no key)Ollama, LM Studio, llama.cpp or vLLM on your PC or your network: free, nothing leaves your place.
MeshyPremium picture-to-3D (optional, Meshy subscription).
DecartThe Live mode of Avatar live, billed per second.
FigmaImport Figma layers into the Library and Templates.

Network keys (X, Telegram, YouTube, Instagram, TikTok) go into Connected accounts: see Connect your accounts.

Choose the engine for each job#

  1. Open Settings › Provider defaults. The image to video, avatar and voiceover rows say which key serves them and whether it is set.
  2. News summarizer and Schedule planner each pick a text engine: a built-in one (Anthropic, OpenAI, Gemini, Ollama), a free provider or a local server. "Automatic" takes the first engine that is ready.
  3. Further down, each configured engine has its Default model row: pick from the list read from the provider, or type a name. Test checks that the model is published, without spending anything; Save applies it at once.

The choice is written to the app's settings file: it applies to every screen. A model name that looks like a key pasted by mistake is refused and flagged in red.

Default video model

The model new Seedance nodes start with in the Studio. Each node can change it.

Default voice model

The ElevenLabs model of new voiceover nodes.

Add a free provider#

  1. In API keys, scroll down to Free providers (OpenAI-compatible), then + Add a provider.
  2. Pick a preset (DeepSeek, OpenRouter, Mistral, Groq, Together, xAI) or type a name and an https URL. Paste the key.
  3. Read the list asks the provider for its models; keep the ones you need and the default model, then Save.
  4. On the row, Test checks the key, Replace the key sets a new one, Delete asks for a second click (Confirm deletion) and erases the key.

The provider becomes the fl:<name> engine: its models join every text model list (the Vectorlab AI dialog, the roles above). The key goes to the vault and is never shown again.

Connect several local servers#

  1. Under Local LLM (Ollama), the Local servers list starts with your Ollama, set just above.
  2. + Add a server: pick a preset (Ollama, LM Studio, llama.cpp, vLLM); the URL must be on this PC or on your local network.
  3. Read the models fills the list, pick the default model, then Save.
  4. Test says whether the server answers and how many models it publishes.

Each server becomes the local:<name> engine, free, in the same lists as free providers.

Protect your keys in the vault#

  1. Open Settings › Vault.
  2. Choose a master password (at least 8 characters), type it twice, then Set up vault. Your keys are encrypted and leave the plain-text file.
  3. Close removes the keys from memory: nothing paid can go out. Open makes them active again with the password.
  4. Remember on this PC opens the vault on its own at launch, for your Windows session; Stop remembering asks for the password again.

On each row of API keys, a badge tells where the key lives: in the file, in the vault, or vault closed (one click takes you there).

Good to know#

The vault password is stored nowhere: if lost, it cannot be recovered. Write it down, or keep an encrypted archive.

Export archive creates a .dzk file that carries your keys, caps and rates to another PC or your phone, protected by its own password. Import an archive… takes them back.

Settings › Diagnostics shows the status of all keys at once (never their value) and the providers' balances. Each row carries Set up, which opens the section where the key is set.

Get started

Choose your AI models and their route#

You will know how to read a list of AI models: which key is used, what one run costs, and what to do when a key is missing. Five minutes, free; the same lists are used across the whole app.

Two routes for the same model#

Wherever you generate (images, videos, sounds, background removal), the model list is sorted into groups, one per route. You keep all your keys: each list offers every route, and you choose model by model.

With the fal key

A single fal.ai key opens most models: FLUX, Nano Banana, GPT Image, Seedream, Veo, Kling… The label says "via fal" when the same model also exists direct.

With your key

The model paid directly to its provider: OpenAI, Gemini, ElevenLabs, Meshy, HeyGen. Handy if you already have an account and credits there.

Local, free

Some tools run on your PC, such as rembg background removal or plain background: no key, no spending.

Read an option's price#

Each option shows its unit price after the name: $0.04/image, $0.10/s of video, $0.0018/s of sound, /30 images for a video cutout. An option marked price to be measured is paid, but its rate isn't known yet: it is never shown as free.

Before a run, the screen shows the total price worked out by the server for what you ask: an image and its background removal, a 6 s video… Your spending caps check this very amount, see Keep spending under control.

Text engines#

The text engine lists (the Vectorlab AI dialog, the roles of Settings › Provider defaults) gather three kinds of engines. The tooltip of the Vectorlab Generate button says, for the chosen engine, what the call costs.

Built-in

Anthropic, OpenAI, Gemini: paid on your key, a few hundredths of a cent per illustration or summary.

Free providers

The fl:… engines (DeepSeek, OpenRouter…): price to be measured. The cap applies to a per-token estimate, at the dearest built-in rate.

Local servers

ollama and the local:… engines run on your PC or your network: free, nothing is charged.

An "add the key" option#

  1. An option whose key is missing stays visible and can be chosen; it carries the note "add the … key in Settings".
  2. If you run it, the run is refused at once, before any spending, naming the missing key.
  3. Add the key in Settings › API keys (see Connect your keys): it works right away, no restart. Or pick the same option with the fal key.

Good to know#

Model names (Flux 3, Veo 3.1 Fast, Sonilo…) are proper names: they stay the same in French and English.

A run whose price exceeds your cap is refused before the call. The most expensive actions run in two clicks: the first shows the estimate, the second runs it.

Get started

Keep spending under control#

You will know what you spend, set a cap per month and per engine, and decide yourself when a render may go over it. Five minutes, free.

Where to see what you spend#

The dollar badge in the top bar shows the month's total. One click opens Settings › Pricing & budget, where everything is set, from any screen and even when Settings is already open on another section. The fal, heygen and voice badges open API keys instead.

Set your rates and caps#

  1. At the top of Pricing & budget, enter your providers' rates (price of a picture, of a second of video, of a voice character…). The costs shown in Quick, the Studio and the Scheduler become accurate. Save pricing.
  2. Video cap per request limits the cost of a single video generation; Max generated seconds per clip limits its length.
  3. Further down, Monthly caps: one overall cap and one per engine (fal, OpenAI, Anthropic, ElevenLabs, HeyGen, Meshy), in dollars. A bar shows what was spent.
  4. Set Alert at (% of a cap): a banner warns you once a month when a cap reaches that level. Save caps.

When a render would go over a cap#

Before leaving, every paid generation is checked against your caps. If it goes over, a “Monthly spending cap” dialog opens, wherever you are in the app:

  1. “Tirer quand même” (run anyway) sends exactly the same request, once.
  2. “Annuler” (cancel) sends nothing and tells you why.

Actual versus estimated#

Below the caps, the Monthly spend — actual vs estimated table gives one row per engine and per screen: the number of runs, what was estimated, what was actually billed, and the difference.

Actual

The provider gave the exact price (Meshy, HeyGen): that is what counts.

Partly actual

Some runs have their exact price, the rest is still estimated.

Estimated

The provider gives no price: the app counts the quote made at launch.

Good to know#

Spending made from your phone goes into the same record and the same caps, counted once. A free provider is counted on a per-token estimate; a local server costs nothing.

The Studio sends the cost it displays as the request's cap: a render cannot cost more than what you saw before clicking.

Get started

Settings, personas and branding#

You will find any setting, give your content a voice with personas and dress the app in your colours with brand kits. Ten minutes, free.

Find a setting#

  1. Open Settings in the rail.
  2. Type a word in Search settings…: accents and capitals do not matter.
  3. Enter opens the first result, Esc clears the field.

The Settings sections#

SectionWhat you do there
DiagnosticsVersion, disk space used, latest alerts, key status and provider balances.
VaultEncrypt your keys and carry them (chapter Connect your keys).
DevicesPair a phone (chapter Drive it from your phone).
API keysSet and test the AI providers' keys.
Connected accountsLink X, Telegram, YouTube, Instagram and TikTok (chapter Connect your accounts).
PersonasThe tone of your content.
BrandingName, logo, colours: your brand kits.
Caption packOne-click brand labels under the Scheduler's caption editor.
Provider defaultsThe engine of each role, default models, language.
PathsWhere your pictures and renders are stored (button to copy the path).
NewsSettings of the News screen.
AppearanceReduced motion and visual effects.
Pricing & budgetYour rates and caps (chapter Keep spending under control).
Machine transferTake your work to another PC (chapter Move to another computer).

Give a voice with personas#

A persona is a personality: its tone, its audience, its way of speaking. The active persona sets the News scriptwriter, the tone of the prompt generator and the default voiceover.

  1. Open Settings › Personas.
  2. Built-in personas can be read but not edited: duplicate one, or click New persona.
  3. Click a persona to make it active.

Dress the app with a brand kit#

  1. Open Settings › Branding. The kit list shows which one is active.
  2. New kit creates one; Activate makes it the active kit and refreshes the app.
  3. The fields below edit the active kit: Logo…, app name, sub-label, two tagline lines, primary and accent colour. Save brand.
  4. Rename, Duplicate and Delete manage each kit. The active kit and the last kit cannot be deleted: the greyed-out button says why.

The active kit dresses the splash screen, the sidebar, the app's accents and Template renders that use the brand. Reset to deepotus restores the original look.

Good to know#

A Template render keeps the kit that was active when you sent it, even if you switch kits while it computes.

Settings › Appearance › Reduced motion turns off decorative animations; it also follows the Windows setting.

Get started

Work for several brands#

You will run several brands in the same installation (Deepotus, a new brand, a client) without ever mixing them up: each has its own persona, identity, Quick templates, publishing accounts, Library and spending. Free; only the assistant's AI proposals are paid, and their price is shown first.

Create a brand's space#

  1. Open Settings › Brand spaces. Your installation already has one space: Deepotus, which keeps everything you had before.
  2. Type the brand's name, pick its colour, then Create space. The new space is empty and not active yet.
  3. On its row, Define the persona opens an eight-step assistant: what you promote, the audience, the character, tone and voice, the visual world, references, what is off-limits, then the synthesis. Nothing is written until you validate.
  4. Persona identity stores the logo, the mascot, product photos, the palette, fonts and a written style. The prompt engine uses it instead of the Deepotus world.
  5. Click Activate: the whole app switches to this space.

Switch from one brand to another#

Two places, one setting: the Active space menu under the brand card at the bottom of the rail, and the persona menu at the top of Quick. Changing one changes the other, and the Library too. In Quick, the prompt templates, the vibes and the default voice-over become those of the chosen brand.

  1. In Quick, open the persona menu at the top of the screen and choose the brand.
  2. The Prompt templates reload with the space's templates. A new space has none yet: Space templates proposes some from the persona, without AI and for free; tick the ones to keep.
  3. + New persona…, at the bottom of the same menu, opens Settings › Brand spaces to create one.

Publish on the brand's accounts#

Accounts per space

Under the list of spaces, Publishing accounts manages the active space's accounts: several X or Telegram accounts if needed, each with its own credentials. Test checks an account; Connect starts the YouTube or TikTok consent.

The Scheduler follows the space

It shows the active space's posts. In a post, Publishing accounts only offers this brand's accounts.

Never on the wrong account

A client's post cannot go out on a Deepotus account: the app refuses to send it.

Sort files and bill#

Library per space

The header menu shows This space or All spaces. Each render is filed in the space where it was started, even if you switch spaces while it runs.

Spending and cap

Each space's row shows what it cost this month. A monthly cap of its own comes on top of the global cap; 0 means no cap.

Statement for the client

Month statement (CSV) downloads the space's spending, ready to attach to an invoice.

Hand over or archive a client's space#

  1. Export, on the space's row, downloads a .zip package: persona, identity and its pictures, Quick templates, brand kit and the list of accounts. No secret goes in: tokens and passwords stay on your PC.
  2. On another installation, Import a space… creates a new space from the package, never replacing one. The message says how many accounts are waiting for their credentials: enter them again in Publishing accounts.
  3. When a contract ends, Archive puts the space away: it leaves the menus, and its scheduled posts are paused. Unarchive, with Show archived spaces, resumes them.

Good to know#

Only one space is active at a time, for the whole app. A render, a post or a task already started keeps its space until the end.

The app's logo and name never change with the space: they are set in Settings › Branding. The kit chosen for a space is only used for that brand's content.

The active space cannot be archived: activate another one first. There is always at least one space.

Get started

Move to another computer#

You will take all your work to another computer, check that nothing got damaged on the way, and get your keys back there. Fifteen minutes, free; the app must be installed on both machines.

What travels#

The transfer takes everything the app created: the Library and the origin of every file, renders, the bible, communication plans, vector documents, card series and 3D models. Your API keys never go into the package.

Export from the old PC#

  1. Open Settings › Machine transfer: the number of files and the size to take are shown.
  2. Click Export…, then pick the destination: a drive, a USB stick, or a path.
  3. Tick the extras if you want them: Logs and Discards — dated trash folders. They are unchecked by default, with their size.
  4. Start export: a dated folder is written at the destination, each file with its checksum. Do not close the app while it writes.
  5. Click Check integrity: every written file is read back and compared with its checksum.

Import on the new PC#

  1. Install the app, then open Settings › Machine transfer and click Import….
  2. Give the package folder, then Check: the app reads the package without writing anything and tells where it comes from (date, machine, version).
  3. Start import. Import adds: nothing this PC already has is overwritten. A damaged file is left out and named.

Take your keys too#

  1. On the old PC: Settings › Vault › Export archive, with a separate password.
  2. On the new PC: Import an archive… and that password. Your keys, caps and rates come back.

Good to know#

Paths from the old machine are rewritten for the new one: your projects find their files without any setting.

Stopping an export leaves an incomplete package. If it happens, run the export again, then Check integrity before importing.

Get started

Drive it from your phone#

You will link your phone to the PC, carry your posts and chapters in your pocket, and cut off a lost phone. Fifteen minutes; you need the Deepotus companion app on the phone and the same Wi-Fi.

Before you start#

By default, the app only listens on this PC: no other device can reach it. To open it to your home Wi-Fi, replace HOST=127.0.0.1 with HOST=0.0.0.0 in the .env file of the data folder, then restart the app. Windows will ask to allow Python through the firewall.

Pair the phone#

  1. Open Settings › Devices. The words this PC only or local network open tell whether the phone will be able to reach you.
  2. Click Pair a device: a QR code appears, valid for five minutes, for a single device.
  3. In the phone app, open Pair and scan the QR code. It closes on its own once read.
  4. To give your keys to the phone, export the encrypted archive from the Vault and open it in the phone app, with its password.

Five devices at most. A paired phone reads what the PC produces; it never sees your keys. It only writes to the PC to drop images and for Avatar live, whose spending goes through your caps.

What the phone does#

Sync

The phone fetches the Library and its pictures, and resumes an interrupted download.

Send pictures to the PC

Your photos land in the Library with the “mobile” source, without duplicates.

The week's batch

Take the approved posts and publish them on Telegram or X from the phone. A post taken by the phone is no longer published by the PC.

Inbox

What you share to Deepotus lands here; pictures go on to the PC.

Offline chapters

Take a chapter, write without a network, hand it back to the PC.

Generate pictures

The cost is shown before each generation, at your PC's rates, and counted in your caps.

Avatar live

Film a take and start a Recast, or open a Live session: the PC does the work, the price is shown first (see Play an avatar).

A chapter taken to the phone#

While a chapter is on the phone, it is read-only on the PC, with a banner. You can force it back to the PC. If the two versions disagree, the phone's text stays in the log, to copy or take back: nothing is lost.

Remove a device#

  1. In Settings › Devices, click Revoke on the phone's row and confirm.
  2. Access is cut right away; the posts and chapters it had taken come back to the PC.

Good to know#

Lost your phone? Revoking is not enough: your keys travelled in the archive. Regenerate them with each provider; the Devices page gives the link to each console.

The phone is notified when a render finishes or fails, when a post is published or awaits an action, and when a cap is near.

Make videos

Make a video in minutes (Quick)#

You will make a vertical video in minutes: an animated clip from a picture, an avatar saying your text, both together, or a voiceover. Paid depending on the provider; the cost is shown before you click.

Before you start#

Quick has four tabs, shown as icons: Seedance (animated clip), HeyGen (talking avatar), Compositing (avatar and clip together) and Voiceover. Hover an icon to read its name; the open tab keeps its label. Just below, the persona menu picks the brand: prompt templates, vibes and voice follow (chapter Work for several brands). A tab stays greyed out while its provider's key is missing: fal.ai for Seedance, HeyGen for the avatar (chapter Connect your keys). The voiceover can also run for free on your PC with Voicebox.

Animate a picture into a clip#

  1. Open Quick, Seedance tab.
  2. Pick the start image: drop it on the area or click Browse thumbnails… to take it from the Library. An end image is optional; if the chosen model does not accept one, the field says so and names the models that do.
  3. Write what should move, or start from a prompt template, or click Open prompt generator.
  4. In Parameters, set the model, the duration and the format (9:16 by default).
  5. Read the estimated cost, then click the Generate button. The render goes through the render queue, top right, and lands in the Library.

With the default model, Seedance 2.5 at 720p, one second costs about $0.47: a 10 s clip comes to about $4.73. A shorter duration or another model costs less; the estimated cost updates with every setting.

Direct the camera#

  1. Unfold Camera (sliders): six sliders (push in, turn, rise…) become a sentence suited to the model, added to the prompt. It is shown before the render.
  2. To choose by eye, click Gallery: eleven camera moves in three styles, as small animations computed on your PC. It is a reminder, not a promise of what the model will do.

Make an avatar talk#

  1. HeyGen tab: pick an avatar and its voice. The lists show up right away, from a copy kept on your PC and refreshed in the background.
  2. For an avatar that looks like you, import a photo: it becomes a talking avatar, selected automatically.
  3. Write the script, then generate. The pauses in your text are kept.

Videos go through HeyGen and its Avatar III engine, picked according to the avatar. The HeyGen balance is shown in dollars. Count about $0.24 a minute at default rates.

Compose and dub#

Composition

An avatar and a clip in the same video, one after the other or side by side (vertical or horizontal split).

Voiceover

Choose the provider for each generation: Voicebox, on your PC and free, or ElevenLabs. A missing provider is refused, never silently replaced.

Music under the voice

When a render has both a voice and music, the music dips on its own under the voice.

Burned-in subtitles

Subtitle the render: aligning a text you provide is free; automatic transcription is paid and only runs if you tick it.

Go further#

Zoom into the preview

The mouse wheel enlarges or shrinks the whole preview card; drag to move it. Double-click or the 0 key: back to 100%.

The voiceover orb

In the Voiceover tab, the preview shows an orb: it breathes at rest, moves while generating and follows the voice's real level during playback.

Presets

At the top of each tab, save your settings under a name and reapply them in one click.

Lip-sync

Syncs the clip's lips to a voiceover (Kling, paid); limits and price are shown beforehand.

Reopen in Quick

Every render keeps its settings: Reopen in Quick, from the Library or the render queue, puts them back as they were.

Extend a clip

From Send to, Extend adds about 7 generated seconds to a clip already rendered, with or without sound; the price is on each button.

Good to know#

Leaving Quick and coming back finds your settings as you left them.

For a still picture, use the Library: Create image, with the Prompt manager. For your own filmed video, Upload video in the Library, then the UGC video node of the Studio.

Make videos

Compose with the Studio#

You will compose a video piece by piece by linking nodes, see it before paying, never pay twice for what is done, and reuse a graph like a recipe. Paid depending on the nodes; the graph's cost is shown before running.

The Studio screen#

On the left, the nodes palette (/ key) and the starter graphs. In the centre, the graph. On the right, the inspector of the selected node, which can be folded. At the top, the graph bar: New, Save, Recipe, Import, the format, Preview, the estimated cost and Run.

Move around the graph#

Drag the background with the middle mouse button to move the view. The wheel zooms around the pointer; the zoom buttons, bottom left, zoom around the centre of the view, from 30% to 150%. The graph always starts below the bar, even when it wraps onto two lines.

The shortcuts box, top right, folds into a badge when a node goes under it: hover it to read it again. Each link lands in the middle of its port's dot; a port name that is too long is shortened, hover it to read it in full.

Compose a graph#

  1. Start from a starter graph (Seedance solo, Avatar post, UGC + animation, News reel post, Timeline montage) or from a blank page with New.
  2. Drag nodes from the palette: sources (picture, text, your video), generators (Seedance, HeyGen avatar, pictures), audio, editing, composition, output.
  3. Link an output, on the right of a node, to an input, on the left of another. Click a node to set it in the inspector.
  4. Preview computes the final composition for free: clips not generated yet are replaced by their picture.
  5. Read the estimated cost, then Run. That amount is sent as a cap: the render cannot cost more. Save keeps the graph under a name.

A first and a last frame#

  1. Wire an Image node that has a file to the Seedance node's end input: that image becomes the shot's last frame, while the image input stays the first.
  2. In the inspector, models that accept a last frame move to the top of the list; the "Slot last frame" line confirms which file is used.
  3. If the chosen model can't take a last frame, a banner warns that the launch would be refused. Its Veo 3.1 Fast (first and last frame) button switches to that model; nothing changes without this click.

The last frame also goes into a Concatenate, a UGC or spatial composition, and from Quick › Composition. Models that accept it: Seedance, Kling v3 Pro and Standard, Veo 3.1 via fal, MiniMax H3, Wan 3.0, LTX 2.5.

Never pay twice for what is done#

The paid render of a Seedance or HeyGen node is pinned automatically: as long as its request does not change, it is reused for free, and the estimated cost says which nodes are.

The last eight renders

The inspector lists the node's last renders; Use picks the one that feeds the rest.

Regenerate

For a new paid take despite the pin, explicitly ask for the node to be regenerated.

Reuse a graph as a recipe#

  1. Recipe freezes the graph: its pictures and texts become blanks to fill in.
  2. Run the recipe with new values: a quote is shown, you confirm. Unchanged nodes are reused for free.
  3. From a picture in the Library, Send to also offers to run a recipe on it.

Go further#

Engine duel

On a picture generation node, the same prompt goes to two models once you agree on the cost; you compare side by side and keep the winner.

Effects and masks

The Effects / Mask node, plugged into the Render's fx input: grades, VHS, colorisation…, on the whole render or a single layer.

AI fields

A field with a coloured edge is sent to an AI. Its badge shows the model and its price; its microphone dictates your text.

Voice and mix

The Voiceover node picks Voicebox or ElevenLabs; Audio mix dips the music under the voice (light, medium, strong).

Brand strip

Link the Brand strip to the Spatial compose's brand input: its text replaces the template strip's text, the logo stays. The inspector preview shows that text.

Import a graph

Import opens a JSON graph; missing sources are listed and nothing is saved without your consent.

Frame by frame

The result drawer steps frame by frame with the , and . keys.

Good to know#

A video generation above the announced cost or your per-request cap is refused before any call. The generated length is capped in Settings; the rest is extended on your PC.

New Seedance nodes start with Seedance 2.5; a saved graph keeps its model. The default model is changed in Settings › Provider defaults.

If the browser cannot dictate, the recording can be transcribed by the server: it is paid, a quote is shown and “No” is the default choice.

Shortcuts#

KeyEffect
/Opens the nodes palette
Ctrl+EnterRuns the graph
, .Previous frame, next frame in the result
Make videos

Reuse templates and brand kits#

You will start from a ready-made layout, touch it up (slots, masks, texts, animations), adapt it to another format and dress it in your brand. Free; only renders of AI-generated slots cost money.

Pick a template#

  1. Open Templates in the rail. The gallery shows a real picture of each layout; the search field filters by name or tag.
  2. Click a card to open it in the editor, or create a blank one with New and a format (9:16, 16:9, 1:1, 4:5).
  3. For the same layout in another format, Reflow to creates a copy with a before / after preview; the original does not change.

Touch up a layout#

  1. Click a slot on the canvas: drag its body to move it, its handles to resize it. The inspector, on the right, shows its settings.
  2. Mask gives a picture or video slot a shape: rounded, ellipse, polygon (triangle, diamond, hexagon, star, or your own points), cut-out windows, soft edge, coloured rim.
  3. Animation brings the slot in and out with a fade, slide or pop, with duration, delay and curve. Replay on canvas shows it.
  4. Add places a text, a ticker, a separator, the brand, a badge or a component.
  5. Save layout, then Open in Studio to fill it in and render it.

Polish the texts#

Ready-made styles

Social subtitle, neon, banner, gradient title; or your own settings: outline, shadow, rounded background, gradient.

Text that fits

The text stays in its slot: it wraps, then shrinks down to a minimum size.

Text on arc

Sets a title as an arch or a smile; an arc too large is reduced to fit.

Exact preview

Renders the slot with the real render engine, to see the final result.

Dress it with your brand#

Templates use your brand kit: name, colours, logo. Kits are managed in Settings › Branding (chapter Settings, personas and branding). A render keeps the kit active when it was sent, even if you switch while it computes.

Go further#

Components

Save as component turns slots into a reusable group; each instance can change its texts and colours, then go back to the component.

Preview sample

A Library picture fills a slot for thumbnails and picture export; never for the video render.

Export

Export image as PNG, JPEG or WebP (it lands in the Library), or as an SVG to drop into Figma.

To the Vectorlab

Open in the Vectorlab opens the layout as an editable vector document.

From Figma

Import a Figma frame… turns it into an editable template; the number of Figma calls is announced beforehand (Figma key required).

Avatar in the right format

A HeyGen avatar is generated in the format closest to its slot: no empty band, no cut-off head.

Good to know#

In the Studio, the layout node shows the transition planned by the template as long as you do not pick another. The “cyan flash” transition is a real colour flash, of your choice.

Make videos

Tell a story in episodes#

You will turn a text, a chapter or a novel into a narrated, illustrated video, scene by scene, and prepare its storyboard before paying for any render. Free up to narration and pictures; their cost is shown beforehand.

Two ways of working#

Open Chapters in the rail. The original flow (Episodes) goes straight from text to narrated video in four steps. The Chapter Workshop is the full space: manuscript, bible of characters and places, screenplay, storyboard, animatic.

An episode in four steps#

  1. Script and voice: give a title, paste the text or upload a .txt, .docx or .pdf. Pick the voice and language, then Generate narration: the whole chapter is read and stored in the audio Library.
  2. Scenes: split the text by paragraph (word for word) or by AI (into visual beats, with an illustration prompt). Edit, reorder, add or remove scenes.
  3. Illustrations: one picture per scene, with the model of your choice. For each scene, pick the animation: slow camera move (Ken Burns), real Seedance clip or still picture.
  4. Assembly and export: a quote gives the price of the Seedance scenes, then the episode is cut on its narration. If a Seedance scene fails, it falls back to a camera move and you are told.

At the top, New, Open and Save manage your episodes; a dot marks what is not saved. Narrate scenes never pays again for a scene already narrated with the same text, voice and language.

The Chapter Workshop#

The Workshop is not translated yet: its buttons below are quoted as they appear, in French.

  1. Script: write or import the chapter text; Manuscrit imports a whole novel, split into chapters, and fills the bible. Recognised names are highlighted.
  2. Bible, on the right: characters, places, objects, dates, moods, sets. Each entry has its description, its picture sheet and, for a character, its voice and temperament.
  3. Screenplay: Adapter (IA) (adapt with AI) rewrites the chapter as a screenplay without touching the manuscript; Voice-over has each scene read by its character's voice.
  4. Storyboard: Découper (IA) (split with AI) or Paragraphes (paragraphs) creates the shots, with their framing, camera, duration and the entities in them.
  5. Animatique (animatic) cuts the shots into a rehearsal video, silent and free, to watch before paying for a render. It then goes into a new Edit project, as a full film or a 30 s reel.

From storyboard to 3D with SAM 3#

  1. In the Storyboard tab, a shot with a production image or a sketch offers the Rebuild in 3D (SAM 3) button.
  2. Name the objects to isolate, separated by commas (the shot's entities are suggested), and pick 3D objects or 3D human body. The price shows beforehand: $0.02 per request.
  3. Rebuild: each object becomes a 3D model placed on the shot's Stage, the first as the subject, the others as set dressing. Open the Stage takes you there.

Frame on the Stage, capture start and end#

  1. Place the camera, then add at least one Keyframe; a second one, later in time, gives the motion.
  2. Capture start / end saves the image of the first and last keyframe to the Library.
  3. Apply to shot… shows what will change (shot type, camera move, start and end images); confirm to write it to the shot.

Generate the shot's video#

The card's Generate the shot (video) button shows the start image (the Stage's first frame, production image or sketch) and the end image if there is one. With an end, only models that accept a last frame are offered, Veo 3.1 Fast first. The cost comes from a free server estimate, refreshed whenever the model changes; it also says when the model generates longer than the shot. Generate the video starts the render: the card follows its progress, then plays the clip.

Go further#

Versions

Every time the text is overwritten, a copy is kept (ten at most): compare, restore, copy.

Exports

The manuscript as .docx or PDF, the screenplay in industry format, the storyboard as a PDF with four shots per page.

Import a screenplay

A Fountain or Final Draft file replaces the scenes (the old screenplay is kept) or is added after them.

Production picture

A shot's picture is generated with the characters' views as references; the cost is stated and confirmed.

Appearances

A bible entry lists its mentions, shots and scenes; one click opens the shot in the storyboard.

To an episode

Épisode (episode) creates a narrated episode (one shot, one scene) without paying anything; narration and render then start in Episodes.

Good to know#

Rewriting a selection in the bible's tone, generating a production picture or adding the animatic's guide voice is paid: the cost is always stated and confirmed first.

A chapter taken to your phone is read-only on the PC, with a banner; see Drive it from your phone.

Make videos

Sound, voices and visual effects#

You will generate music, sound effects and a voiceover you direct, store and find your sounds, and add free visual effects. Each generator's price is shown; visual effects and post-processing are free.

The Sound & VFX screen#

Open Sound & VFX in the rail. At the top, the generators and their price: music, sound effects (606 bundled sounds, plus generation from a description), voiceover, particles and post-processing. Below, three tabs: Audio, Particle VFX and Post-processing.

Direct a voiceover#

  1. In Directed voice-over, write the text.
  2. Click emotion or acting tags (four at most): they go at the start and the Eleven v3 model performs them. The screen shows exactly what is sent to the model.
  3. Generate voice. Trim, add a fade, dip the music under the voice or normalise, then Send to Montage.

Outside the v3 model, or with Voicebox, the tags are removed and you are told.

Music and sound effects#

Music

Instrumental or sung: describe the style, write the lyrics section by section (a skeleton is suggested from the persona). Billed per second, under your caps.

Sound effects

Describe the sound and its length: two variations to listen to, which join the Library and the editor's Sounds drawer.

Voice and music mix

Mixes a voice and a piece of music, dipping the music under the voice; the mix lands in the Library.

A character's voice

In the Workshop, a character gets a cloned voice (paid) and a temperament, performed on each of its lines.

Sound effects: pick a model#

The Generate SFX card of the SFX rail, like the Generate tab of the Montage's Sounds drawer, has a Model list: ElevenLabs direct or via fal, Sonilo, Mirelo, Stable Audio, each with its price per second and its maximum length. Describe the sound, set the length (0 lets the model choose), then Generate: two variants go to the Library. A model via fal runs in two clicks, the first shows the price.

Add sound to a video#

  1. In the Montage, select a video clip on the timeline, then open the Sounds drawer and its Generate tab.
  2. The From the video block names the clip. Pick the model: Sonilo (with "Keep the voice"), Mirelo, Kling, Hunyuan Foley or ThinkSound; some ask for a description of the sound.
  3. A first click gives the estimate, the second runs it. The sound effect goes to the Library; if the model returns the video with sound, it goes there too, under Renders.

AI VFX: relight, remove, reframe…#

  1. In the AI VFX rail, pick the source video among your finished renders.
  2. Pick an action: relight, insert a scene, remove a person or an object, day to night, water, colorize, edit with a sentence, change the format, upscale, or a ready-made effect from an image. Each action states its price and what it needs.
  3. Estimate, then run: the first click shows the server estimate, the second, Run for real, runs it. The rendered video goes to the Library and can be placed in the Montage.

The same actions, except the effect from an image, are in the Montage's effects rack, AI section.

The Sounds drawer#

All your sounds live in the Sounds drawer: in the Library (Audio tab) and in the editor (B key). Filter by kind (effects, voices, music, imported), between your sounds and the bundled catalog, search by name or tag.

Enhance

Equaliser, noise reduction, compressor and normalised loudness in one click, on your PC, no provider.

Split into stems

Splits music into vocals, drums, bass… (paid, quote on first click); each stem stays linked to its parent.

Isolate the voice

Removes the background from a voice take (paid, quote on first click).

Search by description

Describe what you want to hear; sounds similar to a sound can be listed too. Needs the local search service, otherwise the button says why it is greyed out.

Preview

Hover a sound to hear it (option to turn on); Space plays the selected row.

Free visual effects#

  1. Particle VFX: explosions, smoke, sparks, magic… simulated on your PC, to place on a shot.
  2. Post-processing: 16 mm grain, glow, glitch, aberration; applied at render time by the Studio's Render node.
  3. In the editor's effects rack, an effect can go behind the shot's cut-out subject, or in front of it. Cutting out the subject is paid; a first click gives the quote.

Good to know#

Split, isolate, cut out: a first click arms the action and shows the price, a second one starts it, Esc disarms. Nothing goes out without that second click.

Make videos

Play an avatar, deferred or live#

You will learn to create a Character from a few photos, have that Character replay a video in another setting, and film yourself on your webcam transformed live, with their voice. Twenty minutes. Everything is billed per second: the price shows before each launch and counts against your caps.

Before you start#

The Avatar live screen opens from the rail. It needs keys depending on what you do: fal for Recast, the setting and Live, ElevenLabs for the Character's voice. A Decart key is optional: it adds fast mode to Live. The free local voice needs an NVIDIA graphics card and Voixbox (see Install and train a local RVC voice).

Only clone your own face and voice, or those of someone who has agreed to it. The app makes you confirm this for every Character and keeps the date.

Create a Character#

  1. Characters tab: give the Character a Name.
  2. Drop one to eight photos of the same face, front-on and well lit (512 px recommended). They are the reference for Recast and Live.
  3. Tick the consent box (“I have the right to use this face and this voice…”) then click Create the Character.
  4. Optional: Clone the voice with one to five clips of the voice alone (30 s to 3 min in total). Cloning goes through ElevenLabs.

Recast: replay a video#

A 3 to 30 s video keeps its acting; the Character, the setting or an element changes. The render takes a few minutes and joins your renders.

  1. Recast tab: drop the source video, or pick a render from the app.
  2. Choose the Model: its price per second is shown next to it.
  3. Choose the Character, then a setting from the Presets or a free instruction (preferably in English).
  4. Tick the Character's voice if you want the take's voice converted into theirs, at the same pace.
  5. Read the quote under the button, then Start the Recast.

To try at half price, click 480p draft: if you like it, “Finalize in 720p” on its card reruns the same Recast with the same seed. The final render is very close to the draft, without being identical. The motion transfer models have no draft.

Only one person is replaced per take. For the setting, Suggest an instruction from the take has the vision AI connected in your keys describe the place (never the people); read the instruction before you start.

Live: your webcam, transformed#

  1. Live tab: the Provider is fal as soon as your fal key is set (Decart if you have its key). Paste a missing key here, then Save the key: it goes to the vault, the page never sees it.
  2. Choose the Character (or keep your face), a Setting, the Format and the Reserved duration.
  3. Choose the Voice sent: your own as it is, the Character's through ElevenLabs (about 2 s delay), or a local RVC voice (under a second).
  4. Start the live session. The transformed picture appears next to your webcam; switch settings on the fly with Apply the setting.
  5. Record the live session keeps the footage in your renders, ready for the Editor or a Recast.

When a voice is converted, the picture is delayed by as much as the voice: lips and sound arrive together. The live bar shows the converted segments, the latency and any losses.

Going further#

Background only

The subject of the video is cut out, then placed on a color, a Library image or a video. Check the cut-out first shows one picture on the new background; the video only goes after that.

Change only the voice

Keeps a video's picture and replaces its voice with the Character's. Billed at the ElevenLabs character equivalent.

In the Studio

The Recast and voice conversion nodes plug into an existing render or a UGC video. The graph quote counts their price before Run; the Recast node also has its 480p draft.

On the phone

The companion app starts a Recast (480p draft included, then its final version), films a take or opens a Live session, at your PC's prices and under the same caps.

Good to know#

Live is reserved up front, by the minute; only the time actually played is billed. With fal, the app holds the connection: it cuts off at the reserved duration, cuts off as soon as the page closes, and measures the billed seconds itself. With Decart, the cut-off happens at Decart.

A tab hidden for 60 s stops the live session, so you don't pay for nothing. Prefer Edge or Chrome: they can delay the picture to match the voice.

Make videos

Install and train a local RVC voice#

You will learn to install Voixbox, record your voice, train it with RVC and have it speak during a Live session, on your own graphics card. Free: nothing goes to the Internet. Allow thirty minutes to install, a quarter of an hour to record and about an hour of computing per voice.

Before you start#

You need an NVIDIA graphics card with 6 GB of memory or more, and about 6 GB of disk. Without one, Live offers your voice as it is or the Character's voice through ElevenLabs (paid, nothing to install).

The engine is RVC (MIT license), through its official WebUI: the same install trains a voice and makes it speak. Only clone your own voice, or that of someone who has agreed to it.

Install Voixbox (once)#

  1. Open PowerShell in the app folder, where tools\voixbox lives (by default %LOCALAPPDATA%\DeepotusVideoGen).
  2. Run powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File tools\voixbox\installer.ps1.
  3. The script installs uv, downloads a verified version of the WebUI, creates its Python, adds torch for CUDA (about 3 GB) then its weights (560 MB).
  4. It ends with CUDA True | NVIDIA …: the card is detected. On any failure, it stops and says why.

Record your voice#

The quality of the cloned voice depends almost entirely on this recording.

  1. Record 10 to 15 minutes of your voice alone: no music, no second voice, no echo.
  2. A quiet room, the mic 15-20 cm away, always the same mic. Speak the way you do on your live sessions, with varied sentences.
  3. Avoid clipping. Prefer several 30 s to 2 min files, in WAV.
  4. Put them in a folder that holds nothing else, for example C:\Voix\oli.

Train an RVC voice#

  1. Run powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File tools\voixbox\webui.ps1. The WebUI opens in French at http://127.0.0.1:7865; keep the PowerShell window open.
  2. « Entraîner » (Train) tab, step 1: a short experiment name with no spaces or accents (oli), rate 40k, pitch guidance Oui (yes), version v2.
  3. Step 2: your recordings folder, and the rmvpe pitch algorithm.
  4. Step 3: save every 25 epochs, 200 epochs in total (100 for a first try), batch 8 (or 4 with 6 GB), small final model at each save: Oui (yes).
  5. Click « Entraînement en un clic » (one-click training). Allow about 1 h 15 for 200 epochs on an RTX 2080 Ti.
  6. Put the voice where Voixbox looks for it: powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File tools\voixbox\ranger-voix.ps1 -Nom oli.

Listen to it before using it: in the WebUI's « Inférence du modèle » (model inference) tab, pick oli.pth and give it a short recording. A crackling voice needs more epochs or a cleaner recording.

Speak with it during a Live session#

  1. Run powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File tools\voixbox\lancer.ps1 and keep the window open: it reports how many voices are trained.
  2. In Avatar live, Live tab, choose the local RVC voice under Voice sent.
  3. Set Transpose (semitones) if needed: +12 to go from a male to a female voice.
  4. Start the live session. Each half-second of voice is converted in about 110 ms; the picture is delayed by 0.75 s to stay in sync with the lips.

Good to know#

The Live screen tells you what is missing: no NVIDIA card, Voixbox not started, or no trained voice. Another port is set with VOIXBOX_URL in the .env.

With Avast or an antivirus that inspects connections, always go through the scripts in tools\voixbox: they remove the SSLKEYLOGFILE variable for themselves only and read Windows certificates. Otherwise Python crashes (no OPENSSL_Applink).

Make videos

Edit a video#

You will place your shots on a timeline, cut them, move them and chain them, with the gestures of a professional editor. Free: editing and previews run on your PC.

The editor screen#

At the bottom, the timeline: titles (T1), overlays (V2), main video (V1), then dialogue (A1), music (A2), sound effects (A3) and subtitles (S1). In the centre, the viewer; on the right, the inspector of the selected shot. At the top, Preview (free 480p preview), Render and Publish. The bottom bar switches between three views: Media, Edit and Delivery.

Place shots#

  1. Open the media drawer: all your finished video renders, with thumbnail, length and origin. Filter by origin (Studio, Chapters, Quick…), by title or by rating (three stars and up).
  2. Click a media item to place it at the playhead. The edit mode decides how: overwrite, insert and push the rest, at the end, above, ripple overwrite, or fill the range.
  3. From the Library, Send to › Edit also places a video on V1 with its sound on A1. A Studio render or a Chapters episode opens straight in the editor.

Cut and adjust#

Cut

The blade (Alt+C) cuts the shot at the playhead. A gap is selected with one click and Del closes it.

Roll, slip, slide

Alt + drag the diamond moves the cut; Alt + drag the centre slips the content; Shift + drag moves the shot between its neighbours.

Range and markers

I and U set an in and out range; Shift+X cuts it on every track. Shift+M sets a marker, Ctrl+M lists them.

Everything undoes

Ctrl+Z and Ctrl+Y over fifty steps: shots, mix, tracks, subtitles, range, markers.

Cut at scene changes

Right-click a clip: the app spots each scene change and cuts it for you.

Shots too long

In the menu › View, the timeline highlights shots that run too long and jump cuts from the same source.

Chain two shots#

  1. Click the diamond between two shots: the gallery opens, with 58 transitions sorted by family (fades, slides, wipes, zooms, pixels, shapes).
  2. The same panel shows the last frame of the left shot and the first of the right one; shift the cut frame by frame.
  3. For a quick fade on the selected shot: Alt+T. Simple fades play live; the others after a Preview.

Cut out with the model of your choice#

Select a clip: in the inspector, the clip's effects stack offers the subject cutout row, with its list of models and their price (Bria, VEED, Pixelcut, SAM 3.1 that tracks a named subject…). The first click on Cut out (fal) shows the estimate, the second cuts out. The cut-out subject then serves the effects placed behind it; Cut out again starts over with another model.

Organise your projects#

The menu lists every action in six sections, with its shortcut. Projects… opens the grid of your projects: open, duplicate, rename, delete, or compare two versions. Before opening another one, an unnamed edit is put away safely on its own.

New edit

An empty project, with its default tracks, and nothing else.

Copy between projects

Ctrl+C on a clip, Ctrl+V in another project.

Auto-clips

From a long video, AI suggests 1 to 8 excerpts of 15 to 60 s, then creates a project with the chosen one (paid; a free version without AI exists).

Your shortcuts

The ? panel lists the shortcuts; a “Resolve” preset aligns them with DaVinci Resolve. Export them and import them back.

Shortcuts#

KeyEffect
SpacePlay / pause
Alt+CBlade: cut at the playhead
I / URange in / out at the playhead
Ctrl+Left / RightSwap the shot with its neighbour
OFold the tools bar
B / TSounds drawer / Narration panel
G / FSafe zones / viewer full screen
Make videos

Grade, mix and add titles#

You will give your shots a consistent colour, check them on the scopes, set their speed and framing, add titles and polish the sound. Free: everything is computed on your PC, except subtitle transcription and translation.

Grade a shot#

  1. Select a shot: the inspector shows the Grading panel.
  2. Wheels: shadows (lift), midtones (gamma) and highlights (gain). Curves: up to sixteen points, on the whole picture or each colour.
  3. Mask limits the setting to a rectangle or an ellipse, feathered or inverted.
  4. Auto removes a colour cast; Match to previous clip aligns the colours with the shot before.
  5. Copy grade then Paste grade carry the setting over to another shot.

When playback stops, the viewer shows the shot's real graded picture; during playback, the picture stays raw.

Check on the scopes#

Scopes opens a movable window: waveform, vectorscope and histogram of the graded picture under the playhead, recomputed when playback stops. They account for speed, stabilisation and the render frame rate, and stay available in full screen.

Effects, speed and framing#

The effects rack

Noise reduction, deflicker, debanding, sharpening, green-screen keying, monochrome, per-band hue and saturation, trails, lens distortion.

Speed and ramp

From 25 to 400 %. Interpolation smooths the motion; Split at playhead gives the rest of the shot another speed.

Stabilise and reframe

Stabilisation analyses a shaky shot; framing picks the part kept: centred, following the motion, or manual; dynamic zoom animates a reframe.

Adjustment clip

On track J1 (Shift+J), its effects apply to everything below, with fade in and fade out.

Overlays

Position, scale, rotation and opacity animated by keyframes, rounded corners, drop shadow.

Hand-drawn ramps

An effect ramp can follow a Bézier curve you draw; the shake's ramp raises or lowers its amplitude.

Titles and subtitles#

  1. Shift+T places a title card on track T1, burned in at render time.
  2. Pick its template (full frame, lower third, caption, counter, chapter, quote, hashtag, call to action), its text, colour and font.
  3. Subtitles have one track per language: only one is burned in, the others are exported. Translation can create a new language track.

Polish the sound#

The audio rack

Six-band equaliser, noise reducer with adjustable floor, 50 / 60 Hz hum removal, stereo pan; listen to the rendered result.

Learn the noise

Set a range on a stretch of noise only: the app learns it and removes it at render time.

Voiceover from the mic

voice-over (Alt+R) records a take while the edit plays and places it on the dialogue track.

Narration

The narration panel (T) writes and synthesises the voice block by block; only “Narrate” sends a block to the provider.

Good to know#

In the menu › View, the shot lightbox shows every V1 shot with its graded picture: one click goes to the shot.

Subtitle transcription and translation are paid; the rest of this chapter is free.

Make videos

Deliver: renders and formats#

You will export your edit in the right format, at the right loudness, and send it to the Scheduler or to another program. Free: rendering happens on your PC.

Render the video#

  1. Click Render in the top bar: the render panel opens.
  2. Pick the preset: master 1080, web 4K, social 720, ProRes 422, H.265, WebM, audio only (AAC, MP3, WAV) or GIF 480. The project's format is kept.
  3. Set the frame rate (24, 25, 30 or 60 fps) and the loudness: −14 LUFS for YouTube and TikTok, −16 for a podcast, −23 for broadcast. A badge compares the last measurement with the target.
  4. Render starts the render; Add to queue puts it behind the others. To export only the I/O range, tick the box provided.
  5. When it is done, a banner offers to send the video to the Scheduler, with your channels, a date and a prefilled caption. Nothing is published without you.

The Delivery view#

The bottom bar › Delivery lists the project's renders and previews, their status (queued, running, done, failed), and leads to the Library. Publish sends the last final render back to the Scheduler.

Go further#

Your own presets

Save this setting… keeps your output setting as a preset of your own, listed with the others.

To another program

› Project › Export EDL… or Export FCPXML… to take the timeline into DaVinci Resolve or Final Cut.

True to the timeline

The render lasts exactly the timeline, frame for frame; a fade is centred on the cut with the source's real frames.

Good to know#

Run a 480p Preview first: it is free and shows transitions, effects and mix.

Publish

Plan and publish your week#

You will fill your week with posts, review them, approve them in one go and let them go out on time on Telegram, X, YouTube, Instagram and TikTok. The Scheduler is free; only what you produce (image, clip, avatar) has a price, shown before the run.

Before you start#

For a post to go out on its own, its network must be connected: see Connect your accounts. Without a connected account everything still works in assisted mode: the post is ready at the set time and you click Send.

The week at a glance#

Open Scheduler in the rail. At the top, the calendar in Week or Month view. Click a post: its graph (render, caption, one node per channel) shows in the middle and its inspector on the right. The screen fits the window from 1280 to 1600 px; the toolbar wraps when needed.

Fill the week#

  1. Generate plan: describe the week in one sentence, pick the number of days, posts per day, language, start date and channels, then Generate. Without an AI key the built-in planner does the job; with an Anthropic key or a local Ollama model the plan is finer.
  2. Review the proposal, then Add to calendar. Times follow your per-channel time slots.
  3. Already have a written schedule? The Import doc tab turns a .md, .txt, .docx or .pdf file into dated posts, keeping weeks and themes.
  4. For a single post: New post, or add post at the bottom of a day. Episodes from Chapters land here as drafts.

Prepare a post#

In the inspector, set the day and time, tick Scheduled (unticked, the post stays a draft), pick the channels and write the caption, the same on every channel, with its character count. Produce with chosen source makes the visual or clip the plan calls for; the render runs in the background and its thumbnail appears on the graph's Render node.

The final preview shows the post as it will look on the network. For a Reel, a Short or a TikTok, it darkens the top and bottom bands and the right rail that the network's interface covers: put nothing important there.

Approve and publish#

  1. Each post has a mode. Assisted (default): at the set time it flips to ready and you click Send. Auto (Auto-publish at time): it goes out on its own on its connected channels.
  2. Approve the week then Approve the 7 days switches the drafts and scheduled posts of the next 7 days to automatic in one go. A post without media is skipped and named; really editing an approved post puts it back on hold.
  3. To publish right now: Send now on the graph, or the yellow inspector button that counts the channels.

Before each send, the network's quota is checked (X 500 posts a month, Instagram 100 per rolling 24 h, YouTube 100 a day, TikTok 15 a day); a channel already published is never published again.

Going further#

Time slots

Time slots: local times per channel, separated by commas, then Save. Suggest from my metrics picks the hour with the best engagement, from 5 measured posts.

Analytics

Views, likes and engagement over the last 28 days by channel, format and week, with the top 5. Metrics are re-read every day; Refresh now re-reads 10 posts.

Campaign brief

Campaign › Campaign brief: objective, key messages, fixed sections and banned terms. The next plan follows it; banned terms are removed from captions and hashtags.

Recurring series

A rule (days, time, channels, caption template with {date}, {weekday}, {week}): Create series, then Create 4 weeks. These are drafts; creating twice duplicates nothing.

Suggested recycling

Your best-measured posts, published more than three weeks ago, come back with a varied caption. Suggest for tomorrow creates a draft; no paid AI is called.

X thread

Follow-up (X thread) writes the follow-up to an X post: it goes out two minutes later and replies to the previous message, never before it.

Duplicate, sign

Duplicate to next day copies the post. Under the caption, a row of emojis and the Telegram Premium pack insert your brand tags, set in Settings.

With the phone

Approved posts form a batch the paired phone can take along. A post handed to the phone says so in the inspector, with "Take back on the PC".

Good to know#

After an action (approve, create a series, suggest a recycle, add a follow-up), the list reloads by itself: no need to leave the screen.

The calendar, built-in plans, approval and sending are free. Producing an image, a clip or an avatar is paid, under your spending caps (see Control your spending).

Publish

Connect your accounts#

You will plug in Telegram, X, YouTube, Instagram and TikTok so the Scheduler can publish on its own. Free: all it takes is the access each network provides, stored on your PC.

Where it is set#

Open Settings › Connected accounts. One block per network shows how many keys are set and its live status: auto (the Scheduler publishes alone), assisted (it preps the post and you click Send) or not connected.

  1. Expand the network's block and read its note: it says where to get the access.
  2. Paste each value and click Save next to it. The adapter is active right away, no restart.
  3. Check with Verify credentials (or Send test message for Telegram).

Network by network#

Telegram

The simplest, in five minutes. Create a bot with @BotFather, make it an administrator of the channel, paste the bot token and the channel chat ID.

X

The four keys from developer.x.com (API key and secret, access token and secret). The free tier allows posting, up to 500 posts a month.

YouTube

Create a Google OAuth client of type "Desktop app", paste its ID and secret, then Connect. Until the Google project passes the audit, YouTube keeps Shorts private, and the Scheduler says so.

Instagram

A business account and a Page token (EAA…) or Instagram token (IG…). Reels are uploaded from your PC, no hosting, up to 100 posts per rolling 24 h.

TikTok

A TikTok for Developers app (Login Kit, "Desktop" platform): paste the client key and secret, then Connect. Without an audit, uploads are private and the account must be too; set TIKTOK_AUDITED to true after the audit.

Connect YouTube and TikTok without copying a code#

Connect opens the network's consent page in a new tab: accept, come back, the status turns to connected and the refresh token is saved on its own. The same gesture exists in the Scheduler: the Accounts button, then Connect YouTube or Connect TikTok. That panel also shows each network's quota for the month.

Good to know#

A network that is not connected blocks nothing: its posts switch to assisted mode and you send them in one click, or from the phone.

Publish

Follow the news and turn it into posts#

You will follow your news feeds, let the free ranking sort today's articles, and go from article to scheduled post with the daily pipeline. Sorting, filtering and preparing are free; AI and illustrated reels are paid, on request only.

The News screen#

Open News in the rail. On the left, your sources; in the middle, the ranked articles; on the right, the Compose panel. What you ticked, the query, the sort, the voice, the length and the script are back when you return to the screen.

Choose your sources#

  1. Add: paste the address of an RSS or Atom feed. Defaults restores the bundled pack (crypto, geopolitics, economy, politics).
  2. A source's switch pauses it without deleting it.
  3. Refresh all re-reads every feed. The screen also does it on its own, once a day. Pickups of the same wire story are merged into a single article.

Today's ranking#

By default, articles are sorted by Today’s score, a free score: your brief's words, pickup by other outlets, a readable article. The reason and the score show on each card; Most recent sorts by date.

Trending

A topic picked up by three outlets the same day is marked trending, in green on the card.

Already covered

A topic close to a reel launched in the last 30 days is marked in amber, title on hover, and moves down the ranking. An overused source moves down too.

Dropped

The dropped chip counts the articles the filter removed; hover it for the reasons. Show all shows the full ranking, Top only goes back to the first five.

Rank with AI

Rank with AI re-ranks the batch with a language model: paid, under your caps, and only when you click.

In Compose, Campaign brief says what matters today and steers the score. Free filter sets the keywords (empty: everything passes), blocked words and sources, and freshness in hours (1 to 720); Save filter re-ranks at once.

From article to post: the daily pipeline#

  1. Click Daily pipeline. Pick the reel format, the number of articles and the channels. Each format's cost shows before any run: animated cards are free, rendered on your PC; AI illustration, video shots, avatar and voice-over are paid.
  2. Prepare (free) assembles the batch without any paid call: ranked articles, draft script, caption ending with its sources (outlet, date, domain), Scheduler slot.
  3. If needed, Polish with AI rewrites the script (paid). If the spending cap stops the polishing, the draft is kept.
  4. Review the script, caption and slot, then Schedule batch: the post lands in the Scheduler, with its cards reel rendered for free. Nothing is written or spent before that click.

Going further#

X signal

X signal reads recent X posts on your brief: on click only, three times a day at most, counted in your X read quota.

Voice by topic

With Auto (by topic), the persona's tone is picked from the topic's words, for free, and the reason is shown.

To the Studio

Tick articles, then Send to Studio to build them yourself in a graph (see Compose with the Studio).

Good to know#

Everything paid on this screen (rank with AI, polish, X signal, illustrated reels) goes through your spending caps; without a key, the button says so instead of firing.

Images and drawing

Organise and find your media#

You will be able to find any image, sound or render, file it in a project, send it to the screen that needs it and clean up without losing anything. Everything is free and stays on your PC, except captions by a vision model (paid, quote shown).

The Library screen#

Open Library in the rail. At the top, one tab per kind: Images, Renders, 3D, Sprites, Audio, Favorites and Workbench, where a model's versions are listed in lineage order. Everything the app produces arrives here: generators, Photolab, Vectorlab, uploads, phone.

  1. Source chips say where each asset comes from (Generator, Materials, Uploads, mobile…). One click filters.
  2. Tag chips are counted; “3+” keeps images rated three and up. Each image also gets its dominant colour: the hue chips (twelve hues and neutral) filter by colour.
  3. Sort by Most recent or by size, then Grid or list: the list has ten sortable columns (name, source, size, date, dimensions, tags, rating, favourite, licence, hue) and a row opens the sheet.
  4. Each thumbnail shows the file's size and age; the star sets a favourite without opening the sheet, and the dots recall the rating.

An image's sheet#

One click on a thumbnail opens its sheet. From top to bottom you find:

Rating and tags

A rating from 0 to 5, separate from the favourite, and free tags: type, then Add. Search covers tags.

Parent and children

Parent shows the original image and the relation (crop, upscale, retouch…); children appear as clickable thumbnails.

Rights

Licence (suggested from the source), author and link, then Save. An unknown licence is flagged in amber: check it before publishing.

File, recipe, uses

Dimensions, weight, format, dominant colour, source; the generator's recipe (prompt, style, model, seed); and every use: renders, posts, bible, shots, projects.

Review comments

Type, then Comment (or Enter). Each comment has a clickable status: to review, approved, rejected; for a sound, the mm:ss moment. They follow the asset when renamed or restored.

Similar images

≈ Similar images shows visually close images, thanks to the CLIP model installed on your PC.

Replay recipe regenerates a generated image with its original recipe, seed included. It is paid: the price is shown and you confirm before the run; the new image arrives at the top of the list.

Send to another screen#

  1. In the sheet, click Send to….
  2. Pick the screen: Studio, Quick (start image), Template, Chapter or Workshop, Editor, Cardforge, Sprite Lab, Scheduler… Three targets are specific to images: Photolab to retouch it, Vectorlab which creates a new document at its size, and Tile Lab which makes it a tile's source.
  3. Library project… files the asset in a project: the ones already holding it are ticked (one click removes it), and ＋ New project… creates one.

File by project#

The Project list at the top of the screen looks at a single project: every tab then only shows its assets. ＋ New project creates one; a project can be renamed or deleted without touching its assets.

Active project

Auto-file here: everything you produce next (images, renders, 3D, sprites) is filed in it. The reminder stays on screen while it is active, and one click stops it.

On the phone

Pin to the phone: a single project is pinned, and it is the one the mobile companion shows.

Project status

The Status button sorts its assets into edited, published, printed or unused.

Search#

The Search button opens the search bar, with three engines:

  1. Text: captions, tags, prompts, recipes, comments and names, ignoring accents and case. Free, instant.
  2. Captions: a vision model describes images that have none, so you find them better. Paid: the quote is shown (images are sent to Google), the cap is checked, then progress counts the images done.
  3. CLIP: searches by meaning (“a lighthouse at sunset”). Install CLIP downloads about 177 MB once, then indexing and search run on your PC, for free, sending nothing.

The Audio tab mounts the Sounds drawer (tags, filters, sorting, actions) above the upload: see Sound & VFX.

Clean up without losing anything#

  1. Deleting an image, a sound or a render moves it to the Trash, never further.
  2. Cleanup shows the weight per kind and groups of exact duplicates. Tick extra copies keeps the used copy (or the oldest); protected copies (favourite, use, project) stay greyed out. Confirm to move them to the trash.
  3. The Trash counts items and their weight, and flags those older than 30 days. Restore puts the asset back with its projects; if its name was taken, it gets a neighbouring name and says so.
  4. Emptying deletes permanently: old items, everything, or a single item, always after confirmation.

Good to know#

Favourites are saved by the app, no longer by the browser: they follow you from screen to screen and through a transfer. Old browser favourites were imported once.

Only Replay recipe and vision-model captions cost money: price shown first, spending caps checked. Sorting, text search, CLIP, projects and cleanup are free.

Images and drawing

Retouch a photo (Photolab)#

You will be able to open an image in Photolab, select it, retouch it, adjust it and send it back to the Library or another screen. Free and offline: every gesture is computed on your PC by the photocraft engine shipped with Deepotus, with the same pixels as the original application.

Open an image#

  1. Open Photolab in the app bar, right after Vectorlab. From the Library, Send to… › Photolab opens the image directly.
  2. With no document, the welcome screen offers New… (Ctrl+N) and Open from the Library… (Ctrl+O). You can also drag a file onto the work area: it enters the Library and opens.
  3. A new document is chosen by category (Photo, Film and video, Mobile, Print, Web) and preset: HDTV 1080p, 4K UHD, Instagram square, Story 9:16, A4 300 ppi…
  4. Each document has its tab; a dot means it has changed. The status bar at the bottom gives the zoom, mode and depth (RGB · 8 bits), size in pixels and number of layers.

The screen follows the Deepotus language, French or English: menus, tools, panels, dialogs and history.

Pick a tool#

The toolbar on the left has twenty slots. A slot marked with a corner holds several tools: right-click or long-press to choose. Each tool has its letter (V, M, L, W, C, I, J, B, S, Y, E, G, O, P, T, A, U, H, Z), and the same letter cycles to the next tool in the group. The strip at the top shows the active tool's settings.

Select

Rectangle and ellipse (M), lasso and polygonal lasso (L), magic wand, quick selection and object selection (W). Shift adds, Alt subtracts.

Crop and measure
