Crop (C): draw the frame, Enter to cut. The eyedropper (I) picks a colour; the ruler, count and notes are in the next chapter.

Paint

Brush, pencil and mixer brush (B), eraser and background eraser (E), gradient and paint bucket (G). [ and ] set the size, a digit the opacity (4 then 5 = 45%).

Repair

Spot healing and healing brush (J), clone stamp (S, Alt+click for the source), history brush (Y), dodge, burn, sponge, blur, sharpen and smudge (O).

Text and shapes

Type (T): click for a line, drag for a paragraph. Pen (P), path selection (A), rectangle, ellipse, triangle, polygon, line and custom shapes (U).

Move around

Hand (H) or hold Space; zoom (Z) or Ctrl+wheel. Ctrl+0 fits the screen, Ctrl+1 shows 100%.

The swatches under the toolbar hold the foreground and background colours: X swaps them, D restores black and white.

Work the selection#

The Select menu holds All (Ctrl+A), deselect (Ctrl+D) and inverse (Ctrl+Shift+I). The engine can also find the subject, the sky, a colour range or the focus area. Modify › Border, Smooth, Expand, Contract and Feather refine the outline; a selection can be saved to a channel and loaded back.

Select and Mask… (Alt+Ctrl+R) refines difficult edges, hair included: seven views (onion skin, on black, on white…), radius, smoothing, feather, colour decontamination, then output to a selection, a mask or a new layer.

Transform#

Free Transform (Ctrl+T) sets an eight-handle frame. A corner scales and keeps proportions (Shift frees them), an edge stretches one axis, outside rotates (Shift by 15°), Ctrl distorts or skews. The strip gives X, Y, width, height, angle and interpolation; Enter confirms. Edit › Transform also offers 90° and 180° rotations and flips.

Finally, the Edit menu holds cut, copy, paste (including paste in place), fill and stroke, content-aware fill, Fade to soften the last filter, and the Search palette (Ctrl+K) that finds any command by name.

Adjust and filter#

  1. Open Image › Adjustments and pick an adjustment: Levels (Ctrl+L), Curves (Ctrl+M), Hue/Saturation (Ctrl+U), Color Balance, Black & White, Exposure, Vibrance, Shadows/Highlights…
  2. The dialog shows a Preview computed by the engine on a copy. In Curves, a click adds a point, dragging moves it, a double-click removes it, per RGB, red, green or blue channel.
  3. OK applies and adds a history step; Cancel leaves the image untouched.

The Filter menu works the same way: blur (including the blur gallery), sharpen, noise, distort, pixelate, render, stylize, plus the Filter Gallery… and its 47 stackable artistic effects. Last Filter replays with Ctrl+Alt+F. The Image menu also gives automatic corrections, image and canvas size, rotation, and Image › Mode to switch to grayscale, CMYK, Lab, duotone, indexed colour or 16 bits.

Save and send#

  1. Save (Ctrl+S) files the image as PNG in the Library, source “Photolab”, with a working file that keeps the layers. It never overwrites: each save is a new file, linked to the original image in its sheet.
  2. Reopened from the Library, a Photolab image comes back with its layers.
  3. Save As… exports to PNG, JPG, WEBP, TIFF, PSD or PCRAFT and downloads it; Save a Copy… leaves the document as is; Export › Quick Export as PNG outputs the image in one click, following your preferences.
  4. Send to… passes the image to another screen, through the Library.

Close (Ctrl+W), Close All and Close Others ask for confirmation on a changed document. Revert (F12) reloads the last save. File Info… holds title, author, keywords and copyright.

Good to know#

What the screen cannot do yet opens in the native application: Open in the native app…, then Bring back from the native app returns the document, layers included.

If the engine must restart, the screen says so and returns to the welcome screen: unsaved documents are lost. Save often. The installer checks every engine file; Help › About Photolab gives its version and licences.

Shortcuts#

GestureShortcut
Undo, redoCtrl+Z, Ctrl+Shift+Z
New, open, saveCtrl+N, Ctrl+O, Ctrl+S
Free transformCtrl+T
Levels, curves, hueCtrl+L, Ctrl+M, Ctrl+U
Tip size, hardness[ ], Shift+[ Shift+]
Search a commandCtrl+K
Images and drawing

Layers, masks and workspaces#

You will be able to work with non-destructive layers in Photolab: adjustments, masks, styles and smart objects, then arrange the screen your way with panels, workspaces, rulers and preferences. Everything is free and computed on your PC.

The Layers panel#

Each layer has its eye, thumbnail and name; double-click the name to rename it. Click to pick, Ctrl+click to add, Shift+click for a range. Drag a row to place it above, below or inside a group. At the top of the panel: a field to filter by name, the blend mode (27 modes), opacity, fill and locks (transparent pixels, pixels, position, nesting, all).

The panel footer creates a layer or a group, links layers, adds a mask, duplicates, merges down and deletes. The Layer menu goes further: new layer via copy (Ctrl+J), group, clipping mask (Ctrl+Alt+G), arrange, align and distribute, merge (Ctrl+E) or flatten, rasterize, matting.

Add an adjustment layer#

  1. Open the Adjustments tab, next to Properties.
  2. Click an adjustment, for example Black & White: an adjustment layer is added above the active layer. The image below is not touched.
  3. Its sliders appear in Properties; Curves and Levels have their own editor there. Come back at any time by picking the layer.

Sixteen adjustments work this way (brightness, levels, curves, hue, colour balance, channel mixer, gradient map…), as well as fill layers: solid colour, gradient or pattern.

Masks, styles, smart objects#

Layer mask

The mask button reveals the selection (or everything); Alt does the opposite. On the mask thumbnail: Shift+click disables it, Alt+click shows it alone, Ctrl+click loads it as a selection.

Vector mask

On a layer that already has a mask, the same button adds a vector mask, or Layer › Vector Mask from the active path.

Layer style

Drop shadow, glows, bevel, stroke, satin, overlays: a dialog with preview. A style can be copied, pasted or cleared; the Styles panel offers ready ones (neon, chrome, gold…).

Smart filters

Filter › Convert for Smart Filters: every filter applied afterwards appears under the layer, with its eye; double-click to reopen its settings, drag to change the order.

A single layer can be exported: Layer › Export As… (PNG, JPG or WEBP, at the chosen scale, to download or the Library) or quick export as PNG.

New AI layer#

  1. Click New AI layer… at the foot of the Layers panel, or in the Layer menu.
  2. Describe the image, pick the model and the layer to place it above; tick Remove the image background for a subject without a background. The total price shows beforehand.
  3. Generate the layer: a pixel layer "AI — …" lands above the chosen layer. Two Ctrl+Z undo it.

Remove a layer's background#

Layer › Remove layer background cuts out the chosen layer without destroying it: the cut-out copy lands on top, the original stays below, hidden, never deleted. The removal model and its price show beforehand; three Ctrl+Z go back.

The panels#

On the right, panels are arranged in tabbed groups; the rail's icon column collapses or reopens each group, and the Window menu ticks the visible ones.

Colour and swatches

Color (F6) with hex code, Swatches (personal groups kept by Deepotus), Gradients and Patterns.

History and info

History: a click on a step goes back to it. Navigator, per-channel Histogram, Info (F8) under the pointer, Channels and their shortcuts (Ctrl+2, Ctrl+3…).

Brushes

Tips with search, Brush Settings (F5), Clone Source and Tool Presets (e.g. soft eraser 60 px).

Text and paths

Character, Paragraph, Glyphs, character and paragraph styles; Paths, Shapes; Layer Comps to switch from one state to another.

Choose a workspace#

  1. Open Window › Workspace, or the list at the top right.
  2. Pick one of seven layouts: Essentials (default), Basic, Graphic and Web, Motion, Painting, Photo, Pixel Art. Panels and tools arrange for the task.
  3. What you move, collapse or hide is remembered for that workspace. Reset restores it; Lock Workspace stops remembering.
  4. New Workspace… saves your layout (up to twenty), kept in the Deepotus data folder.

Rulers, grid and guides#

In View: Rulers (Ctrl+R), Show › Grid (Ctrl+') and Guides (Ctrl+;). Drag from a ruler to place a guide; the Move tool moves it, or removes it by dragging it out. Snap (Ctrl+Shift+;) aligns selections and layers to guides, grid, layers or document edges. Extras (Ctrl+H) hides everything at once.

The same menu offers zooms, horizontal flip of the view (the document does not change), pixel art preview with crisp pixels and screen modes: F goes to the next one, Esc back to standard mode.

Measure, annotate, slice#

Ruler (I)

Drag to measure distance and angle; Alt from an end makes a protractor. Straighten Layer puts the line level.

Count (I)

A click places a numbered mark, Alt+click removes it. Measurements are recorded in the log, exportable as CSV for a spreadsheet.

Note (I)

A note with author and colour, placed on the image; the Notes panel steps from one to the next. File › Import › Notes… copies them from another document.

Slices (C)

Cut the image for the web, or from guides; slice selection moves them, divides them and sets their options (link, alt text).

Preferences and shortcuts#

Edit › Preferences opens eighteen sections, saved in the Deepotus data folder: interface (canvas colour, document border, tooltips), tools, file handling and quick export, cursors, transparency, units and rulers, guides and grid, text. Some sections simply say what Deepotus handles in their place (performance, scratch disks…). The reset button restores all defaults, after confirmation.

Keyboard shortcuts

Change a command's shortcut or a tool's letter; a conflict is named and removed from the other command. Summarize… downloads the list as an HTML page.

Menus and presets

Hide or colour menu entries. The preset manager organises brushes, shapes and patterns; they export and re-import as .json.

Touch screen

Modifier Keys shows Shift, Ctrl and Alt on screen: a click applies to the next gesture, a double click holds the key.

Good to know#

Workspaces, preferences, shortcuts and personal swatches are kept by Deepotus in its data folder: they follow you through a transfer to another PC.

Images and drawing

Draw vectors (Vectorlab)#

You will be able to draw a poster, a logo or a sheet in vectors in Vectorlab: shapes, pen, text, appearance, layers, symbols, then send it to other screens. Free, everything is computed on your PC; only AI illustration is paid, price shown first.

Open Vectorlab#

  1. Open Vectorlab in the app bar. The home lists your documents: one click on a card opens it. Pick a format (square, 16:9, A4, playing card…) then Create for a new document.
  2. A document also comes from elsewhere: Send to… › Vectorlab from the Library or Photolab, “Edit this face in Vectorlab” from Card Forge, “Open in Vectorlab” from a Templates layout.
  3. At the top left, two pills: Vector to draw, Pixel to retouch pixels (see the next chapter). Each has its own tools and panels.

The screen follows Affinity's conventions: ten menus at the top (File, Edit, Document, Text, Vector, Pixel, Layer, View, Window, Help), a context bar showing the selection and the current tool's settings, tools on the left, the tabbed panel stack on the right and a status bar that recalls the tool's gestures. The document tab shows “name @ zoom” and a star when it is not saved.

Pick a tool#

Tools are grouped in families: only the current tool of each family is visible. The corner triangle or a long press opens the family, right-click opens the tool's settings, the letter picks it from the keyboard.

Select (V)

The marquee only takes objects fully inside (Alt: those it touches). Shift constrains, Ctrl resizes from the centre, Alt+drag copies, Ctrl+click reaches an object inside a group, Tab goes to the next one.

Pen (P) and Node (N)

Click = sharp node, drag = smooth node, click the first node to close. Four modes: Pen, Smart, Polygon, Line. The Node tool pulls handles, bends a segment, adds (double-click) or deletes nodes.

Shapes (R, E, L, F)

Rectangle, ellipse, line and parametric shapes (polygon, star, cog, arrow, donut, spiral) adjustable by handles. A single click places a shape; the Corner tool (C) rounds a corner.

Freehand

Smoothed pencil (B), vector brush (J) with flat, tapered or calligraphic profile, eraser (W), knife (X) and shape builder (S) that combines or removes areas by clicks.

Text (T)

Drag = text sized to the height you pull; click on a curve = text on that path; double-click to edit in place. The text frame flows text and flags overflow in red.

Eyedropper, measure, view

Eyedropper (I) with loupe (Ctrl: the whole style), measure (M), hand (H), zoom (Z, Alt to zoom out). Ctrl+0 fits the page, Ctrl+1 shows 100%.

Set the appearance#

  1. Select an object. The context bar gives X, Y, W, H and opacity; fields accept calculations (100/3).
  2. The Appearance tab sets fill and stroke from the swatches, no fill or no stroke, width, opacity. Stroke and Transform have their own tabs (skew, movable pivot).
  3. Appearance + goes further: linear, radial and conical gradients, transparency, patterns (hatching, dots, checkerboard), multiple strokes, six effects, 16 blend modes, global colours, harmonies, object styles, paste inside a shape (clipping mask), text in a frame or on a path.

An offset stroke and a text on a path stay live: they recompute when their source changes, until you detach them.

Layers and symbols#

The Layers tab shows the layer's opacity and blend mode at the top, then each layer with its thumbnail, lock and eye; a triangle unfolds it into a tree of its objects, clips, masks and effects. The Layer menu creates, renames, groups (Ctrl+G), locks, hides and orders.

A symbol is created with Vector › Create Symbol; its instances follow every change. Double-click an instance to edit it in place, then Done or Discard.

Build up layers with AI#

  1. Prepare your layers: for instance a background, an empty layer for the image, a text layer on top.
  2. Select the image layer and click AI image on this layer at the foot of the Layers panel. The panel names the target layer and the model, and offers Remove the background with its removal model.
  3. The total price, image and background removal, shows beforehand. The "Generate on …" button places the image on that layer, below the text. Repeat on another layer for a second image.

An image already placed is cut out from the Image tab: pick the model next to Background, its price shows, then Remove the background. Ctrl+Z brings back the previous image.

The Vector menu#

Geometry

Add, subtract, intersect and divide shapes; join, reverse, break at node; Round corners.

Convert to curves

A text becomes paths (Ctrl+Enter), as one or one path per glyph.

Image trace

Image Trace… vectorises a placed image (colours, smoothing, threshold), with preview, on your PC.

The document#

The Document menu holds Setup… (size, resolution, unit, background), Artboards… exported separately, Margins and bleed… (guides never exported), the Document grid… (square, iso, triangular, hexagonal, snapping), Board and terrains… to paint tiles (K) and the Real map…. View › Snap to objects snaps to edges, centres and even gaps.

File › Place image… or Place from Library… places an image; the Stock tab shows the Library with search, one click places the image. An image can be cropped, locked and also receives effects.

Good to know#

The document is saved as a draft every 30 seconds: when you reopen it, a window offers to restore it or to start from the server. History keeps 1000 steps; Edit › Add Snapshot marks a state to come back to.

Hover an option for a second, or click the “?” next to it, for its animated card. F1 lists every shortcut; Edit › Settings (Ctrl+,) sets tooltips, grid and snapping.

AI illustration (AI family, or File › New image processing) is paid: the price is shown first, within your caps. Everything else is free.

Shortcuts#

GestureShortcut
Undo, redoCtrl+Z, Ctrl+Shift+Z
Duplicate, group, ungroupCtrl+D, Ctrl+G, Ctrl+Shift+G
Fit page, 100%, gridCtrl+0, Ctrl+1, G
Vectorlab homeCtrl+Alt+H
All shortcutsF1
Images and drawing

Pixel art, export, maps and 3D objects#

You will be able to retouch pixels and make pixel art in Vectorlab, export your drawings in the right format, build a map from real data and turn a drawing into parts to 3D-print. Everything is free and computed on your PC.

The Pixel persona#

  1. Click the Pixel pill (or View › Pixel Persona). The same document keeps its layers; tools and panels change. From the Game Assets hub, the Pixel card opens this persona directly.
  2. To retouch a placed image, pick it then Pixel › Edit pixels.
  3. Select pixels: rectangle (M), lasso (L), magic wand (W) or by colour; the Pixel menu grows, contracts or inverts them (Ctrl+I).
  4. Paint: brush (B) and eraser (E) with radius, hardness and round or square shape, paint bucket (G) contiguous or global, clone stamp (C), blur, dodge and burn. Right-click = secondary colour, X swaps them, Alt+click picks.

Pixel › Adjustments and filters… gives levels, curves, hue and saturation, black and white, threshold and blur. Every retouch undoes with Ctrl+Z, like the rest of the document. The Histogram tab shows the four channels of the edited image.

Make pixel art#

The Pixel-art panel sets tile size, symmetry, palette (the same as Sprite Lab and Tile Lab), quantization and the pixel grid. The pixel pencil (K) draws without double pixels in diagonals; Shift+click draws a straight segment from the last point.

Trace a reference

Set as reference fades and locks an image with its grid; a pixel layer sits on top to draw cell by cell, the eyedropper takes a cell's exact, average or dominant colour.

Pixelate

Pixelate turns an image or a vector selection into big pixels. Rasterize adds palette and dithering (ordered or Floyd-Steinberg).

Tiles and seams

The 3×3 preview scores a tile's seams; the 2:1 iso tile limits painting to the diamond, with symmetry along its edges.

Animation

The timeline shows frames: play (Enter), loop, FPS, red (previous) and blue (next) onion skin. Export as a PNG + JSON sheet or a strip.

Finishing

Dark outline sets the drawing off the background, Sharpen boosts contrast; PNG export scales from ×1 to ×16 without blur.

To the other labs

Pixel › Pixel art to Tilelab… sends the drawing to Tile Lab; the Pixel-art panel also sends it to Sprite Lab.

Export#

  1. Open the Export tab (File › Export… or Window › Export), shared by both personas.
  2. Choose what goes out: the whole document, each artboard, each visible layer, each selected object, or the slices drawn with the Slice tool.
  3. Choose the format (PNG, JPEG, WebP, SVG, PDF, DXF) and one or more resolutions (@1x, @2x…). File names build themselves; a batch export outputs every slice, resolution and format at once.

Vector PDF

By default: text as outlines, page at physical size, vector gradients and patterns, crop marks and bleed for the printer. A message says what had to be rasterized and why.

DXF for cutting

In millimetres, text as glyph outlines, symbols and groups included.

Quick exports

File › Export SVG (embedded images), Export PNG 2×, and Send to Bible… for a chapter.

A real map#

Document › Real map… opens the Map panel: no key, no cost, it lays a shaded relief, draws contour lines as vector paths at the chosen interval, adds an OpenStreetMap background with its attribution, and slices the map into hexagonal tiles coloured by altitude. File › Import GPX… places a track at true scale, keeps its altitude (profile, length, climbs) and can turn it into a raised ribbon.

Print in 3D#

  1. File › 3D Print… (or Text › 3D Logo…). Choose the mode: layers (one height per layer), board tiles with base, logo (bevel, hollowing with a minimum wall), map relief, or pixel art (one height per colour).
  2. Set heights and options, then 3D preview: the model turns in the viewer, each part in its colour, with dimensions, triangles and volume. A model wider than the bed is flagged.
  3. One STL for a single part, or Batch per tile / slab: one STL per part, a coloured plateau.3mf and nomenclature.csv. Open the slicer hands over to your printing software.

In relief mode, numbered slabs get sockets under the base and separate keys (0.2 mm clearance) to fit together. Side draft tilts a logo's edges for demoulding.

Good to know#

A text must be converted to curves to be printed: the dialog says so and skips it otherwise. To go further with a 3D model, see the Workbench and 3D printing.

Games and 3D

Make game assets#

You will be able to find your way around the Game Assets hub, turn an image into a 3D model and open the right 2D tool: Sprite Lab, Tile Lab, Vectorlab's Pixel persona or Card Forge. The 2D labs are free and run on your PC; 3D generation is paid, price shown first.

The Game Assets hub#

Open Game Assets in the rail. One tab per tool: 3D (image to 3D model), 3D Studio (see Image to 3D), Assets 2D, Sprites 2D and Tiles (the labs opened inside the hub), Materials (Material Forge) and Cards (Card Forge).

An image becomes a 3D model#

  1. In the 3D tab, pick a source image from the Library: ideally a character or object cleanly cut out on a neutral background.
  2. Pick the engine, from cheapest to most refined: TripoSR, Hunyuan3D, Tripo (default, good value), TRELLIS and Rodin. Only the fal.ai key is needed.
  3. Options: textures, T-pose for a character to animate, multi-view (four views generated first for a more faithful model), and formats: GLB always, plus FBX, OBJ, STL or USDZ depending on the engine.
  4. The total price is shown next to Generate 3D, before the run. The pipeline then shows each step live; the model turns in the viewer, every format and every view can be downloaded.

Models also land in the 3D tab of the Library; the Workbench then prepares them for printing.

Open a 2D tool#

The Assets 2D tab gathers four cards, each with Open and Guide:

Sprite Lab

An image, a video or a sheet becomes an animated sprite sheet, with directions, skeleton, hitboxes and engine exports. See Animate sprites.

Tile Lab

Seamless tiles, blob 47 or 16 tilesets, variants, iso and hex shapes, painted maps, exports to Tiled, LDtk and Godot. See Paint tile scenery.

Pixel — Vectorlab

Opens Vectorlab straight in the Pixel persona: frame timeline, 2:1 iso tile, rasterize an image. See Pixel art.

Card Forge

Playing cards: printer templates, back and registration, languages, batch art, booklet. See Card Forge.

Shared palettes#

Sprite Lab, Tile Lab and Vectorlab's Pixel persona share the same list of palettes: adaptive (N colours), PICO-8, Game Boy, NES, Sweetie 16, 1-bit, Grayscale 16 (sixteen greys) and Handheld 4 (four tones, handheld console style). A palette gives the same result in all three tools. Dithering (ordered or Floyd-Steinberg) softens gradients.

Good to know#

Only 3D generation costs money: the price shown counts each extra view and format, and goes through your spending caps. The 2D labs are free.

3D rendering runs in your browser: keep the tab in front for smooth rotation. Files live in the Deepotus data folder and follow a transfer.

Games and 3D

Animate sprites (Sprite Lab)#

You will be able to build an animated sprite sheet in Sprite Lab: start from a shipped effect, a sheet, a video or a bible character, slice it, align it, pixelate it, then export it for your game engine. Almost everything is free and local; only animating an image and prompt generation are paid, price shown first.

The Sprite Lab screen#

Open Sprite Lab from the Assets 2D tab of the Game Assets hub. Three columns: the source on the left (Get started, Image, Render, Video, Sheet, Bible, Prompt), the extracted frames and settings in the middle, the animated preview and exports on the right.

A sprite in one click#

  1. Get started tab: twelve particle effects (burst, smoke, sparks, aura…) and animated sequences, made from free textures shipped with the app.
  2. One click produces the sheet, the frames, the GIF and the Unity pack, no key, no credit, no network.
  3. The preview plays the animation: Space play / pause, speed 0.5×, 1× or 2×, plain backgrounds or scenes (Sky, Outdoor, Dungeon, Cave), and W A S D or the arrows walk the sprite. The mirror button flips it.

Start from an existing sheet#

  1. Sheet tab: pick a sheet from the Library, or Open a PNG from my PC. Nothing is sent, nothing is spent.
  2. Auto-detect counts columns, rows and occupied cells from transparency; otherwise, set the columns × rows grid yourself.
  3. Drag to paint the cell selection (Ctrl adds or removes, Shift extends), or All, None, one cell in 2, 3 or 4.
  4. Align: Feet puts each character on the same floor, Left / right re-centres, Both axes does both; the arrows nudge the current frame by one pixel, Reset undoes.
  5. Group ranges under a name (walk, jump…) as loop, ping-pong or reverse, then export the Aligned sheet, its JSON, or Copy JSON.

The other sources#

Image, Render, Video

A Library image is animated on a plain background (paid); a render or a video from your PC is sliced into frames. Set sampling, the number of frames and background removal (cloud, local or chroma key).

Bible

4 directions (sheet) cuts a character's south, west, east, north views; 8 directions (3D model) renders its model from eight angles. Free.

Prompt

Describe a sprite, add the persona's words in one click, then Generate the images: the cost is shown first, images are cut out locally and become the source.

Any source also accepts 1 to 64 Library images, taken in order as frames.

Set up the sheet#

In the middle: cell (128, 256, 512 or native, no upscaling), anchor centred or at the feet, columns. Pixel art (9b) reduces to the target size with a shared palette and dithering. Animation: duration per frame and tags (idle, run, jump…) written into every export. Post-processing: outline, drop shadow, orphan-pixel cleanup, edge smoothing. Then Generate the sheet.

Edit, hitboxes, skeleton#

Editor

Reorder, duplicate or delete frames of a finished sheet, then Apply; tags follow. Nothing is redone or paid again.

Hitboxes

Draw per-frame hit (strike) or hurt (can be hit) rectangles, sixteen at most; adjust them, copy them from one frame to another (Ctrl+C / Ctrl+V). They go into the JSON atlas and Paper2D.

Spine skeleton

Draw bones then parts, name them, and Write the rig produces a Spine 3.8 skeleton with its parts.

Export#

Under the preview: Sheet PNG, ZIP (frames and Unity pack, with all engine exports), GIF, Godot 4 resource (.tres), JSON atlas for Phaser and PixiJS, Aseprite file (.ase) and Unreal Paper2D sheet. Save to Library files the sheet in the Library, from where it can be sent to Vectorlab or Tile Lab.

Good to know#

Paid: animating an image (Image tab), cloud background removal and prompt generation, always within your caps, price shown first. Get started, Sheet, Bible, Render, Video with local removal and every export are free.

Games and 3D

Paint tiled levels (Tile Lab)#

You will be able to build seamless tiles, auto-tiling tilesets, iso or hexagonal tiles in Tile Lab, and paint a small map ready for Tiled, LDtk or Godot. Everything is free and computed on your PC.

The Tile Lab screen#

Open Tile Lab from the Assets 2D tab of the Game Assets hub. A bar of five modes: Seamless, Tile sheet, Tileset, Shapes and Painter. On the left, the source (Library images); on the right, the result. An image sent from the Library or Photolab (“Tile Lab — tile source”) arrives directly as the source.

A seamless tile#

  1. Seamless mode: pick an image (floor, wall, foliage texture…).
  2. Method: 50/50 offset with blend (natural) or 2×2 mirror (perfect, kaleidoscope effect); crop and size; optional pixel art with a shared palette.
  3. Make seamless shows the tile, its 3×3 tiling and the seam score before and after (0 = perfect). The tile joins the Library.

Build a tileset#

  1. Tileset mode: click an image for material A (terrain) then a second for B (background). The Material Forge toggle takes the base colour of a Material Forge material.
  2. Choose the set: Blob 47 (eight neighbours, rounded corners) or Blob 16 (four edges, faster), the side in pixels, 1 to 5 variants per tile and the seed.
  3. Build the tileset builds the atlas and measures how neighbours join; the atlas is copied to the Library.
  4. New preview draws a random map where each cell gets the tile of its neighbours; Measure judges seams, visible repetition and lighting (ok / warning).
  5. Export atlas.png then your engine's format: Tiled (.tsx), LDtk (.ldtk) or Godot (.tres), to be placed next to the atlas.

The “Style of a bible location” block composes a tile prompt bound by a location's sheet and palette: Location prompt, then Copy prompt to paste it into the image generator. Nothing is generated here.

Paint a map#

Painter mode, once a tileset is built: set width, height and seed, then click and drag on the grid to paint terrain, go over again to erase. On each stroke, the right tile is placed from its neighbours, and the composed map shows below with carte.png and carte.json. Clear all empties the grid.

Shapes and tile sheets#

Shapes

A material becomes a 2:1 iso diamond or flat-top hexagon tile that tiles without seams. Build the tile shows the tiling; export to Tiled and Godot.

Tile sheet

Open an existing sheet: Detect finds each tile by its transparency, the placement grid (square or 2:1 iso) tests seams, double-click = ×9 tiling.

Sheet exports

Aligned sheet and JSON, tileset and JSON, or Separate tiles (zip); the aligned sheet can also join the Library.

Games and 3D

Create playing cards (Card Forge)#

You will be able to compose a complete card game in Card Forge, from the face to the printer-ready pack, and deliver it to a virtual table with its rulebook. Almost everything is free and local; only illustration generation and translation by a language model are paid, quote shown first.

The Card Forge screen#

  1. Open the Cards tab of the Game Assets hub. Templates offers starter decks (New deck from this template).
  2. At the top, set the format (poker, bridge, tarot, mini, square, domino, business card, jumbo, micro), the resolution (150, 300 or 600 DPI), bleed, safe zone and corner radius. These settings apply to every part and to the export.
  3. On the left, eleven modules; in the middle, the card with its guides, front or back, card by card.

The eleven modules#

01 Face · 02 Frame · 03 Typography

The illustration (imported, generated or taken from the local catalogue), borders, rarity and back, the title, rules and flavour text, with the shipped fonts.

04 Data

The deck comes from a CSV, a Notion export ZIP or a Google Sheets link…; each column feeds a field. The deck statistics (histograms, cost curve) and the “Back” line spot gaps.

05 Volume · 06 Materials

3D preview with real thickness and edge; eight PBR texture channels computed locally.

07 Print

Home sheets or printer templates, preflight, printer pack and duplex test chart (see below).

08 3D Export · 09 3D Forge

A GLB and a glTF with every PBR map; the 3D Forge turns the card into a printable object (see the 3D object).

10 Import · 11 Publishing

Import existing cards; deliver around the card: virtual tables, rulebook, mockup, product sheet.

Edit this face in the Vectorlab opens the rendered face in a Vectorlab document at the deck's physical size, with guides and a locked layer.

Several languages#

Columns suffixed by language (name_fr, name_en…, twelve languages) are recognised: pick the active language and every part follows, with what is missing card by card. Translating a column with a language model is proposed card by card; nothing enters the table without your click, and the quote shows before any call (local Ollama: free).

Print#

  1. Module 07: choose home imposition (A4 or Letter sheets, crop lines or crosses) or the exact template of MakePlayingCards, The Game Crafter or DriveThruCards (bleed, safe zone, DPI, pixels expected by the portal). An unverified format is greyed out and says so.
  2. Preflight re-reads the produced file itself: bleed, crop marks, the PDF's TrimBox and BleedBox, PNG density. Re-check runs it again.
  3. Printer pack (.zip) delivers named fronts and backs, padded to the deck size, with a manifest ready to upload. For DriveThruCards, the PDF becomes X-1a (CMYK) if the press profile is loaded; otherwise the gap is written on screen.
  4. Duplex test chart (PDF) prints two pages with a vernier to a tenth of a millimetre to measure your printer's front-back offset.

Publish and deliver#

Virtual tables

Export for Tabletop Simulator (.zip) (10 × 7 sheets and saved object) or Export for Tabletopia (.zip) (one image per face). Place in Tabletop Simulator copies the deck into your saved objects.

Rulebook

Composed at 300 DPI with the app's fonts (“#” headings) and a card sheet.

Mockup and sheet

Cards fanned out (five at most) in square, story or landscape format, and a product sheet with figures, ready to copy.

Deck art can also be generated in a batch: a template prompt with {columns}, a style, a bible entity; quote per row, cap per batch and your spending caps are checked before the run.

Good to know#

Paid: generating a face or the deck art, translating with an online model, and the 3D Forge's image-to-3D engines. Everything else is free and runs on your PC.

Games and 3D

From image to 3D object#

You will be able to turn a card into a printable 3D piece with Card Forge's 3D Forge, and produce a complete 3D model (mesh, texture, skeleton, animations, formats) in the 3D Studio. Local pipelines are free; image-to-3D engines are paid, price shown before any run.

From card to object: the 3D Forge#

  1. In Card Forge, open module 09 3D Forge then Export layers: background, illustration, veil, frame, typography, ornaments and composite, front and back. The screen proves the stacking (0 px gap) before delivering, and the server checks it again.
  2. Edit the graph: each layer gets a flat or relief treatment (closed solid), a Material Forge material tiled at physical scale, a finish (holographic silver or gold, lacquer, leather, brushed metal, emissive) and a placement. A relief with no depth entered takes its material's physical height, otherwise 0.6 mm.
  3. The “3D mesh” treatment sends a layer to an image-to-3D engine: the price shows on the node and at the foot of the graph before any run.
  4. Build the 3D artifact assembles the final GLB, and an STL if every element is a closed solid; otherwise the refusal says why. The manifest lists elements, engines and credits.

The “Game objects” panel also creates printable 3D pieces: a Token, a Card relief token, a pawn or a stand, plus the Unfolded box (PDF)…, the vector pattern of a tuck box at the deck's thickness.

The 3D Studio#

The 3D Studio (a tab of the Game Assets hub) chains a Meshy graph from prompt or start image to deliverables: mesh, PBR texture, topology, skeleton (auto-rig), animations, GLB, FBX, USDZ, OBJ or STL export, then the Workbench. Each node carries its cost; the series cost shows before Run, and the log follows each task. A Meshy key is needed; fal engines (tripo, rodin, hunyuan, trellis, triposr) use your fal key.

Prepare the views before paying for the mesh#

  1. In the hub's 3D card, the “Views first” block generates the views first (front, back, profiles): a failed view does not cost a mesh.
  2. For free, reuse the views of a bible character's sheet, or build the view set from your photos (phone ones first, straightened and cut out).
  3. Per thumbnail: Remove the background (local, free) or replay a single view with a corrected prompt (paid).
  4. “Run · engine” launches the mesh on the approved views: only the engine is billed.

Rig, conversion, optimisation#

fal workshop

fal workshop (rig a job) lists your 3D jobs: Meshy rig with animations (walk, run…), quote per task; greyed buttons say why (key, approval, texture).

Convert and import

Free local conversion to OBJ, STL, 3MF or glTF (STL and 3MF at a size in mm), or by Meshy to FBX, USDZ, BLEND. Import a model (OBJ, STL, glTF, GLB) makes it a job.

LOD and textures

The Optimise area derives levels of detail with measured loss and mobile, PC, print budgets, and exports textures to Blender, Unity, Unreal or Godot conventions.

Engine bench

The medians measured on your machine per engine (triangles, weight, watertightness, cost); add an existing job to it for free. An optional local GPU service makes Hunyuan free.

Good to know#

Paid: image-to-3D engines (fal in dollars, Meshy in credits), rigging, Meshy conversion and generated views. The price is announced first, the spending table prices rig and refine, and texturing without a fal key is refused straight away instead of failing later.

Games and 3D

Create materials (Material Forge)#

You will be able to create seamless materials in Material Forge, from a free catalogue, a generator, a photo or a description, and export them to Blender, Unity, Unreal or Godot. The catalogue, generators and maps are free and local; only the AI-generated base image is billed.

A material from the catalogue#

  1. Open the Materials tab of the Game Assets hub, then CC0 catalog: thirty free Poly Haven materials in six families (floors, walls and bricks, metals, wood, fabrics and leathers, concrete and terrain).
  2. Pick one or more then import: missing maps are derived locally, the source credit is kept.
  3. The material lands in the gallery with a real 3D preview, its eight PBR maps and its measured seam score. One click reopens it in the editor.

The generators#

The Generators tab offers ten seamless patterns: bricks, tiles, planks, checkerboard, hexagons, pebbles, brushed metal, leather, fabric, stripes. Tune them live, then Create the material. Local and free.

Forge from a description or a photo#

  1. Forge tab: describe the material (rusty iron, frosted glass…) or start from a reference image; pick the resolution (1K, 2K, 4K) and the seam method.
  2. Forge the material: only the base image is billed (price shown on the button); seams, maps and preview are computed locally, recomputable at will.
  3. A raw photo becomes a material: click the four corners of a surface shot at an angle to straighten it, then remove the baked lighting with an adjustable strength (the badge shows the before and after gap). On a phone, the field opens the camera.

Judge and tune#

Environments

Seven HDRIs provided, and your own (.hdr or 2:1 image) to add or delete. Varied gallery meshes: sphere, cube, torus, cylinder, plane, 3×3 tiling.

Compare, My model

Compare opens a second preview, same environment and camera; “My model” puts the material on a Workbench model.

Physical height

The height map declares its millimetres (0 to 20 mm), reused by the card 3D Forge's relief.

Finishes

A preset (lacquer, leather, animated emissive, brushed metal) is tried in the preview before being applied or cancelled. Emission above 1 keeps its hue.

Export#

Each material exports as a ZIP with a manifest, following a naming convention: standard, Blender (Principled BSDF slots indicated), Unity, Unreal or Godot. It also serves as a source in Tile Lab and as a material in the 3D Forge.

Good to know#

Only the base image of “Forge the material” is billed, within your caps. Catalogue, generators, photo, delighting, maps and exports are free.

Games and 3D

Prepare a part before slicing (Workbench)#

You will be able to prepare a 3D part before sending it to the slicer: scale it, repair it, lay it down, check its overhangs, hollow it, arrange it on the bed, then export it to the printer or a game engine. Free and local. Nothing is irreversible: every gesture that changes the part writes one more version, and all of them stay on disk.

Open the Workbench#

In the 3D Studio, click the 07 · 3D Workbench node; the Workbench takes over the page, and 3D Studio at the top left brings you back. On the left, the model's life lists each model and its versions: one click loads a version, Alt+click compares it (A/B view). On the right, four tabs: Parts, Rig, Report, Export. Help opens this chapter's step-by-step and glossary.

The main gesture#

  1. Set a target size. target size field: the largest wanted dimension, in millimetres (80 for a figurine, 250 for a board). A 3D file carries no unit: while this field is empty the Workbench shows “glTF units” and refuses whatever needs a physical dimension (hollowing, arranging, exporting for print). A refusal beats an invented millimetre.
  2. Pick the printer. The Elegoo Centauri Carbon 2 profile is built in (256 × 256 mm bed, 256 mm height, one excluded area); installed OrcaSlicer or ElegooSlicer profiles show up too, read, never modified, and you can enter one by hand. On the plate, the green outline is the real bed, the red rectangle the area where nothing may sit.
  3. Repair. Report tab, Repair in one click: coincident vertices welded, duplicate faces and flat triangles dropped, normals unified. Capping holes is unchecked by default: it adds material. The detail appears in the bottom bar.
  4. Lay the part flat. Place on a face (F), then click the face that must touch the bed. The gesture joins the queue, and write the version saves it. If unsure, Orient proposes three ranked poses (support, overhang, height) in the Report tab. A computed orientation does not always find the best pose: always review the proposal, no score knows which face you want to look good. If the queue holds both a placement and a recentring, the bar flags the contradiction and greys out writing.
  5. Look at the overhangs, then the slices (see below).
  6. Hollow it, when it helps. Report, Hollow, 2 mm wall to begin with: the solid inside becomes a shell. It is first a resin (SLA) gesture; with filament (FDM), the slicer already fills the inside. It needs a closed mesh, and the Workbench states the thickness that holds when the requested wall is too thick. For resin, then drill a drain hole: Drill (drain hole), 3 to 4 mm, then click the face, preferably near the bed. The drill goes through the one wall under the click and stitches the hole closed.
  7. Arrange on the bed, measure, then export (see below).

The order that works: repair, lay down, inspect, hollow, export. Repair first, because every other gesture starts from sound geometry, and hollowing refuses an open mesh.

Look before slicing#

Overhangs paints orange the faces leaning less than 45° from horizontal: there, a layer has almost nothing under it and the slicer will add a support. Re-lay the part until the orange recedes. Slices draws twenty cross-sections in blue to see the real shape at each height. Both are indicative previews: nothing is written, and the slicer does the real slicing.

The Report tab#

Decimate, extract

Decimate reduces triangles towards a target and says if it is not reached; extracting one by one splits each element into a sibling version.

Materials

Colour, opacity, metal, roughness, emission, alpha mode and double side, with preview; only the touched fields are written.

Measure

Measure: two clicks give a distance, its x/y/z components and the angle between the two faces, drawn in the scene.

Parts, booleans, connectors#

Booleans

Parts tab: A = selection, B = selection, then union, difference (A − B) or intersection and Apply. The bar states the seam and lost materials.

Cut and assemble

The Knife cuts the part; its bar adds a connector: dowel (holes and a separate pin), plug and its socket with clearance, or a sliding dovetail.

Skin

A Material Forge material on the ticked parts: Skin. Masks shows cavities (red) and edges (green) in view B.

The Rig tab draws the skeleton through the skin, highlights a bone's chain, colours its influence weights, rotates a bone with three x/y/z sliders and plays the shipped animation clips.

Arrange on the bed#

On the plate separates the pieces, then Arrange on the bed lays them inside the real bed, rotated when that saves room, 2 mm apart, on up to eight beds; what does not fit is reported. Drag a piece (snapped to the bed grid, Shift frees it), nudge it with the arrow keys: its position, size and angle are shown. The plate is a view: it is saved, but it does not change the model.

Export#

  1. Export tab, 3D printing: the STL and 3MF of the displayed version, at the target size in millimetres (see 3D-print your creations). Open in the slicer takes you there.
  2. For an engine: Prepare writes one glTF per target (Blender, Godot, Unreal, Unity) with its import sheet; dropping copies it into the engine project; Open launches Blender or the project; Back from Blender re-imports a fixed GLB as one more version and says what was lost.

Glossary#

The words your slicer will use, explained once.

TermWhat it is
Base (bed contact)The face that touches the bed. Wide and flat, the print holds; narrow, it comes loose.
OverhangA wall leaning too far to rest on the layer below. Prusa puts the clean limit without support between 45 and 60° from horizontal.
SupportA disposable structure holding overhangs up. The slicer generates it; the Workbench only helps you need less of it.
BrimA one-layer collar around the part, to keep its corners from lifting.
RaftA platform printed UNDER the whole part. Safer than a brim, costlier, and it leaves a rough face.
SkirtAn outline drawn next to the part, not touching it, to prime the flow before starting.
InfillThe pattern inside. Gyroid is about equally strong in every direction; Lightning only supports top surfaces. 15 % is usually enough.
SeamEach wall loop starts and ends somewhere, leaving a visible vertical line. The slicer places it (Nearest, Aligned, Rear) or scatters it (Random).
RetractionFilament pulled back during travel moves, to avoid strings (stringing).
LayerA horizontal slice. 0.2 mm is the usual compromise; 0.12 mm for detail, 0.28 mm for speed.
Perimeter (wall)The number of wall loops. Two perimeters at 0.45 mm make a 0.9 mm wall: the minimum to aim for when modeling.
BridgingPrinting a layer over empty space, between two supports. It works over a few centimeters, with good cooling.
WarpingCorners lifting as they cool. Remedies: clean bed, brim, closed enclosure. Common with ABS/ASA, rare with PLA.
WatertightnessA solid is watertight when its surface is closed, with no hole or free edge. That is what the Workbench bar calls "fermé" (closed).
ManifoldEvery edge belongs to exactly two faces. A mesh can be closed and still be hard to slice cleanly if it is not.
DecimationReducing the triangle count. A 500,000-triangle mesh prints no better than a 100,000 one, but slows everything down. Report tab › Decimate.
HollowingReplacing the solid inside with a shell of given thickness. Mostly useful in resin; 2 mm is a good starting point.
Drain holeThe hole(s) letting uncured resin (and air) out of a hollowed part. In the Workbench: Report tab › Drill (drain hole).

Numeric settings (temperatures, speeds) apply to the hardware they name; on another machine they are starting points, not truths. Two repair tools often recommended elsewhere, Microsoft 3D Builder and Autodesk Meshmixer, are no longer maintained, so they are not listed here.

Games and 3D

3D-print your creations#

You will be able to send everything the app produces to your 3D printer: generated models, Workbench parts, 3D Forge cards and Vectorlab drawings. Everything is local and free: no provider call, and the app never generates G-code.

Before you start#

The pipeline is designed for the Elegoo Centauri Carbon 2 (256 × 256 × 256 mm bed) and its slicer ElegooSlicer, shipped with the machine; OrcaSlicer works too. Install the slicer once: Windows associates .3mf files with it, and Open in the slicer uses that. Without an association, the app tells you; then set SLICER_PATH (the slicer's path) in the data folder's .env file.

Each export writes a folder in DeepotusVideoGenData\assets\print3d\: the STL (the mesh), the 3MF (the one you open, in millimetres and named) and impression.json (provenance, scale, watertightness).

Where to export from#

  1. From the Workbench: Export tab, 3D printing writes the displayed version (repaired, laid down, hollowed…) at the target size. It is the recommended path: see Prepare a part.
  2. From Game Assets · 3D: each generated model has its 3D printing button. Give the largest dimension in millimetres (80 for a figurine); the part is centred and placed on the floor. The file “optimised” for game engines is refused with a message saying what to take.
  3. From the cards' 3D Forge: when every element is a closed solid, the manifest delivers an STL and the print button appears. Leave the size empty to keep the card's real millimetres. Watertightness is marked guaranteed there.
  4. From Vectorlab: File › 3D Print… turns the drawing into parts: one height per layer, tiles, a bevelled logo, a map relief or pixel art. See 3D printing from Vectorlab.
  5. Slice in the slicer. The 3MF opens at the right size, laid on the bed. Supports, fine orientation, infill, filament profiles: that is the slicer's job. Above 256 mm, the export warns you without blocking you.

Good to know#

The watertightness of meshes from image-to-3D engines is marked unknown in impression.json: ElegooSlicer and OrcaSlicer repair small defects on import and report it. Go through the Workbench first to repair in one click. Only the cards' 3D Forge guarantees its solids, through its “closed solid” check.

Games and 3D

Stage shots on the 3D Set#

You will be able to block a shot in 3D on the Stage before any paid run: place volumes or a real mesh, frame at the film's format, set a camera move, then send it all back to the storyboard shot. Free and local.

Compose the scene#

  1. From a shot card of the Workshop storyboard, the Stage button opens that shot's scene; Workshop brings you back.
  2. Place simple volumes: Box, Capsule, Cylinder, Sphere, or a mesh from a 3D job or a bible entity, chosen in the list (grouped under “Bible entities” and “3D meshes”) then placed with the button next to it.
  3. Each object has a name, a role (subject, set dressing, marker), a position, a rotation, a scale and its measured dimensions; Duplicate or Remove.

Frame and animate#

Frame

16:9, 9:16, 1:1 or 2.39:1 format, focal length in millimetres, guides (thirds, crosses, title safe, horizon). The shot type (wide, medium, close-up) is measured from the subject's height in the frame.

Motion

K places a camera keyframe at the playhead; a preset lays a dolly-in, a 90° orbit, a crane down or a locked-off shot. Space plays the move in a loop.

Outputs#

  1. Capture start / end: the frame of the first and last keyframe goes to the Library, with its provenance.
  2. Compose the GLB: the scene's GLB, versioned with its sheet.
  3. Apply to shot…: proposes to the linked shot the shot type, the move, the motion prompt and the end images, compared before and after; nothing changes without your confirmation.

Good to know#

The Stage is for deciding before paying: the captured end images become the start and end frames of a video shot, and the measured move feeds its prompt.

Reference

End-to-end recipes, from idea to post#

You will be able to chain screens to go from an idea to a published or printed result. Each path points to the chapters that detail every step; any cost is announced before each run.

An image, then a post#

  1. In the Library, describe the image then Create image (paid, price shown), or upload your own.
  2. Retouch it if needed in Photolab: Send to… › Photolab, then Save.
  3. Send to… › Scheduler creates a post draft; the Scheduler sets caption, channels and slot. Nothing goes out without your click.

A reel from the news#

  1. In News, let the free ranking sort today's articles.
  2. Daily pipeline: pick the reel form (animated cards are free), then Prepare (free).
  3. Review the script and caption, then Schedule batch: the post lands in the Scheduler with its reel.

An episode of your novel#

  1. In Chapters, paste your chapter; the Workshop derives the breakdown, the bible and the storyboard.
  2. Block the tricky shots on the 3D Stage before paying for any video.
  3. Assemble the episode, finish it in the Editor (titles, mix, subtitles), then deliver in each network's formats.

A printed card game#

  1. In Card Forge, start from a template, import your data (CSV, Google Sheets, Notion) and set the format.
  2. Retouch a face in Vectorlab if needed (“Edit this face in the Vectorlab”).
  3. Module 07: pick your printer's template, let preflight re-read the file, then export the printer pack. The 3D Forge adds tokens and a box.

A 3D-printed figurine#

  1. Pick a cleanly cut-out image and generate the model in the 3D tab of Game Assets (paid, price shown), or prepare its views for free first.
  2. Open it in the Workbench: target size, repair, lay down, check overhangs, arrange on the bed.
  3. Export › 3D printing, then Open in the slicer: see 3D-print your creations.

Assets for your game#

  1. Animate a character in Sprite Lab and export the sheet for Unity, Godot or Phaser.
  2. Build a tileset in Tile Lab from two materials, paint a map, export to Tiled, LDtk or Godot.
Reference

Read the icons#

You will recognise an icon at a glance, find its name, and print the full sheet to keep next to your screen. Free, no key needed.

One icon, one function#

The whole app speaks the same language: the Deepotus Glyph set, 526 icons drawn with the same stroke. Each one stands for a single function: the same drawing means the same thing in the editor, the Photolab or the Card Forge. The old emojis and symbols are gone from buttons, menus and lists.

  1. Rest the pointer on a button: its tooltip gives its name and, if it has one, its keyboard shortcut.
  2. Look that name up in the icon sheet to read what it does and what not to confuse it with.
  3. In the Vectorlab, the Photolab, the Sprite Lab and the Tile Lab, wait a little longer (900 ms) or click the small ? button: an animated card SHOWS you the option.

Icon families#

Icons are sorted into families. Knowing the family already tells you what to expect when you click.

Navigation

A screen, a tab or a panel: you go there, nothing is changed.

Actions

A button that does something: create, save, send, delete.

Editing

Change something already there: align, flip, group, lock.

Tools

The drawing and retouching tools of the labs.

Layers and adjustments

Layers, masks, styles and image adjustments.

Media and playback

Play, cut and edit video and sound.

States

What the app tells you, without you having to click.

Categories

Content families, each with its own colour.

3D

Objects and actions of the 3D workshops.

States worth knowing#

A state icon is not clicked: it informs you. These are the ones to read before starting a paid render.

IconWhat it says
Done: the render, the upload or the save worked.
In progress or waiting: loading, generating, or queued.
Failed: the tooltip or the message next to it says why.
Warning: nothing is broken, but read before going on.
Spending limit close or reached: beyond it, the app refuses the spend and asks you what to do.
Generative field: AI can fill it in for you.
Locked: nothing can move, change or delete the item while it is.
Pinned (Studio): this node result is reused for free on the next render.

Print the icon sheet#

The icon sheet shows them all, sorted by family, with their name, their function and the look-alike icons not to confuse them with.

  1. Open the icon sheet.
  2. To print only part of it, click a family (for example Vectorlab tools) or type a word in the search: only what is shown gets printed.
  3. Click Print: each family starts on a new A4 page, black on white. You can also download the full sheet as a PDF.

On the sheet, the red line starting with “≠” names the look-alike icons: Close hides a window, Delete destroys, Remove takes something out of a list without destroying it.

Animated cards in the labs#

In the labs, some options have an animated card in three beats made of real screenshots: the starting point, the gesture, the result. It opens when you rest the pointer on the option for 900 ms, or with the ? button next to it (in the Sprite Lab and the Tile Lab, even when the option is greyed out). Here they all are; cards of labs not yet translated still show the French interface.

Good to know#

The icon of the app, of its shortcuts and of browser tabs is the real Deepotus logo. Inside the app, the logo shown follows your active brand kit (chapter Templates and brand kits).

Troubleshooting#

You will be able to recognise the most common messages and know what to do. Always start with Settings › Diagnostics: version, disk space, latest alerts, key status (never their value) and provider balances, at a glance.

Symptoms and fixes#

SymptomWhat to do
A button says a key is missing, or a provider pill is red at the top right.Add or fix the key in Settings, keys section (see Connect your keys). It works straight away, no restart.
A generation is refused: cap reached.The window says which cap blocks and offers to adjust it. See Keep spending under control.
The HeyGen avatar list takes a while to appear the first time.Normal on the very first load: the list is long. It is then kept on disk and shows instantly.
An ElevenLabs voice returns a plan error.On ElevenLabs' free plan, only “premade” voices work through the API. Pick one, or move to a paid plan.
Certificate error (CERTIFICATE_VERIFY_FAILED).An antivirus inspects HTTPS. The app uses Windows' certificates and handles it on its own; otherwise, turn off the antivirus's HTTPS inspection.
“Port 8765 already in use”.The app is already running: open http://deepotus.localhost:8765.
After a restart, my keys or Library seem “gone”.Nothing is lost: everything lives in %LOCALAPPDATA%\DeepotusVideoGenData. Start the app again from its Desktop icon.
Photolab returns to its welcome screen with an engine message.The retouching engine was restarted; unsaved documents are lost. Save often (see Photolab).
A 3D file is refused at print export.Go through the Workbench: set a target size and repair in one click before exporting.
I deleted an image by mistake.It is in the Library Trash: Restore.

Where are my files?#

In %LOCALAPPDATA%\DeepotusVideoGenData\assets: images for images, outputs\final for rendered videos, outputs\uploads for your uploads, audio for sounds, print3d for print exports. To take everything to another PC, see Move to another computer.

Good to know#

An app message always says what blocks and how to fix it. If a button is greyed out, hover it: its tooltip says why.

Deepotus Video Gen v2.8.0 — guide built from the real app. Everything runs locally on your machine; only calls to providers (fal.ai, HeyGen, ElevenLabs…) go over the Internet, with your own keys.
